Designed 2026-08-14, revision 3. **This was NOT in memory and I failed to find it when
asked — that is why it is here now.** Artifact:
https://claude.ai/code/artifact/e9a8f908-bcae-4f22-b4e0-ba5be33cb417

**The problem.** `entity_relationships` is one graph table with **six independent
writers**, two trust levels, and no enforced boundary. It is also the locked authz
substrate (June): principals are entities, memberships are `member_of` edges, ACLs are
`can_read`/`deny_read` edges, one SQL gate reads all of it. So "links for everything, up
to row and column level" is the direction ALREADY CHOSEN — the work is to finish it.

**Built vs designed:** built = `member_of`, Slack/GitHub ACL sync, resource read gate,
`$resource` registry. NOT built = `can_read`/`deny_read` (zero occurrences on
origin/main), boolean ACL expression compiler, freshness/`aclSupport` state, connector
`acl`/`principal`/`membership` records.

**The constraint that bounds "links for everything": edges are inherently OR.** Two
`can_read` edges mean "either audience may read". Real rules need AND, and expressing AND
as two edges silently WIDENS access. The answer is not smarter traversal — compile the
expression to an effective principal BEFORE it becomes an edge; if a source cannot be
compiled safely it is `aclSupport: none` => owner-only, fail closed.
- Resource-level read: YES, built. Row-level: YES (a row is a finer resource).
- Intersectional (A AND B): only via the unbuilt compiler.
- **Column-level: BREAKS OUTRIGHT.** Post-gate masking is UNSAFE — by then the value is
  already in search text, embeddings, prompts, summaries, exports, caches, logs. Use
  **facet events** (sensitive field as a separate finance-only event pointing at the same
  entity), not masking.

**Spikes (measured, not argued):** dropping the live-triple unique index is READ-safe
(gate is `EXISTS`, 0 of 23 read sites do single-row-per-triple lookups) but breaks THREE
`ON CONFLICT (from,to,type)` writers (`access-graph`, `channel-about`,
`github-team-graph`). 3-hop customer->quote->invoice->payment over ~1000 edges = **18 ms**
(performance is not the constraint). **The agent SQL tool rejects `WITH RECURSIVE`** —
agents get bounded hand-written traversal only; separate product gap.

**Escalation path traced (not executed):** `$links` has NO approval branch and NO mutation
gate — `entity-mutation-gate.ts` guards only update and never mentions `link`; the approval
branches in `manage_entity.ts` (346, 597, 781, 1397) all sit OUTSIDE the link handler
(1463-1571). With `validateTypeRule` permitting any pair when no rules are seeded, an agent
holding `manage_entity` in an ACL-synced org can assert an access-granting edge. Wants a
real security review.

**Two defects found:** the locked plan cites `member_left_channel` for fast revocation but
`SLACK_BOT_EVENTS` does NOT subscribe it (bounded-revocation SLA depends on a mechanism
that does not exist). And `entity-management.ts:1027` issues a **hard `DELETE FROM
entity_relationships`** — a third mutator class any consolidation will miss.
`buildAccessGraph` is treated as atomic but takes no transaction (`access-graph.ts:280,378`).

**Settled sequence:**
1. **Gate `$links`** — smallest diff, highest urgency, no gate exists today.
2. Claim-aware relationship store; migrate all six inserters + merge repointing + tool
   unlink + the hard DELETE; rewrite the three `ON CONFLICT` upserts.
3. `assertion_key` column + index move (read-safe; fixes channel-about, ACL
   over-deletion, merge, multi-connector assertion). **APPROVED by the user 2026-08-15**
   — the amendment to the locked decision is signed off, so this no longer blocks. Build
   order is unchanged: it is still step 3, AFTER gating `$links` (step 1) and the
   claim-aware store (step 2). Approval is not permission to start here.
4. Connector domain-edge rules in `afterPersist` + a feedless directory lane for
   `principal|membership|identity`.
5. The locked authz program as its own track, starting with the Slack revocation gap.

**IT ALREADY IDENTIFIED THE CONNECTOR EDGE GAP.** "The gap that is actually open" =
**domain knowledge edges** (invoice belongs_to order, order fulfils quote, product in price
list) — no authorization meaning, the substance of an imported business system, and *"the
word relationship does not appear in the connector SDK"*. Proposed
`interface EntityRelationshipRule { key: string; ... }` with ONE safety rule, not a tier
system. **I re-derived this same gap from scratch on 2026-08-15 — do not derive it a third
time; it is step 4 above.**

Out of scope deliberately: a separate claims table (only if the live-triple index proves
immovable); field masking as post-gate projection (replaced by facet events); recursive
traversal for agents (real gap, but query-surface not edge-model).

Not covered by the spikes: the demo had zero `order`/stock-movement/journal-entry rows, so
the full 5-hop chain was never traversed; row-level `can_read` cardinality was estimated,
not measured.

===== project_entity_write_hook_design.md =====
---
name: project_entity_write_hook_design
description: "Settled direction for ERP-style write rules: project-authored onWrite hooks run in an isolated-vm INSIDE the write transaction; core ships only funnel + hook + gapless-ordinal capability, zero domain vocabulary"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T00:41:16.853Z
---

Decided 2026-08-14/15. Supersedes the interceptor approach that was built and is
being DISCARDED (see [[project_erp_gap_branches_status]]).

**The model.** Project-authored hooks, co-located on the entity type, run in a V8
isolate INSIDE the write transaction:

```ts
const postingRules = (ctx) => {           // plain function — reuse across types
  if (ctx.op === "update" && FROZEN.has(ctx.current.status)) return ctx.deny("frozen");
};
defineEntityType({ key: "invoice", properties: {...}, onWrite: postingRules });
```

**Why transaction-local hooks work.** The historic objection to untrusted code in a
transaction is unbounded runtime pinning a connection. Running the hook after row locks
means **TOCTOU disappears** and the versioned-precondition / CAS scheme drafted earlier
is unnecessary. `isolated-vm` v6 (Node 22-24) / v7 aliased as `isolated-vm-next`
(Node 26+) already ship in `packages/server`; `run-script.ts` disposes the isolate to
terminate, uncatchable by the guest.

**CODEX REJECTED TWO PARTS OF THIS (2026-08-15) — do not rebuild on them:**
1. **No in-process tenant code in the gateway.** The gateway holds the transaction and
   locks; a **separate, credential-free executor process** runs the pure synchronous
   code. Failure path: kill and replace the helper, roll back.
2. **"Bounded by construction" is FALSE as stated.** A CPU budget does not bound
   wall-clock transaction hold time. Every phase needs its own deadline — cardinality,
   byte, queue, execution AND wall.
Verdict: "The transaction-local hook idea is no longer fundamentally wrong", but only
with those two corrections plus DB constraints as the final backstop, and hooks stay
disabled until the funnel has zero production bypasses.

**Core surface — three mechanisms, ZERO domain vocabulary.** No `lifecycle`,
`periodClose`, or `numbering` keys: those are core smuggling accounting back in as
config. Core provides only:
1. the write funnel,
2. the hook (locked `current` + normalized final `candidate` + `deny` + `patch` +
   a platform-prefetched declared read set),
3. a gapless-ordinal allocation capability the hook *requests* (allocation is the one
   thing a guest cannot be trusted to implement).

Shared implementations like a state-machine helper belong in a **project-level library
that compiles down to an onWrite** — "shared code" and "core code" are not the same
thing.

**Build order — the funnel FIRST.** A hook without a chokepoint is worse than nothing:
documented as an invariant while `entity-merge.ts`, `entity-link-upsert.ts`,
`classifier-extraction.ts` and `member-entity.ts` walk past it. Then approval/invariant
separation, then merge as a first-class op (not delete+update), then the hook.

**Authoring — do NOT co-locate a closure on the entity type.** I proposed
`defineEntityType({ onWrite: fn })`; codex rejected it and is right: `defineEntityType`
is intentionally a plain-data producer, and **a closure cannot be serialized** —
lexical bindings, imports and captured consts are not preserved by `Function#toString`.
Use a separate artifact with a FILE reference and data bindings:

```ts
defineEntityWriteHook({
  key: "ledger-write-rules",
  targets: [{ entityTypes: [invoice, payment, journalEntry],
              operations: ["create","update","delete","merge","unmerge"] }],
  reads: { period: entityByUniqueKey({ entityType: accountingPeriod,
             key: ["ledgerId","period"], lock: "share", maxRows: 1 }) },
  handler: writeHookFromFile("./hooks/ledger-write.ts"),
});
```
The type may reference the hook handle as optional sugar. The read-set DSL must expose
only indexed, statically bounded platform ops — never arbitrary SQL — each with max rows,
max bytes, lookup keys and lock mode; absence/set predicates must declare a coordination
strategy or be rejected at install. Install mirrors connectors + Behavior reaction files
(`desired-state.ts:943`). Persistence: immutable hook versions (source, artifact hash,
runtime ABI, declared capabilities), materialized active bindings keyed
`(org, entity_type, operation, order)`, atomic active-version pointer, disable+rollback.
Read bindings by index — never derive "latest" by scanning history.

**`unmerge` must be first-class too** — already implemented at `entity-merge.ts:450`;
hiding it behind update/delete recreates exactly the hole merge has now.

**More bypassers than previously recorded:** entity-link upsert, classifier extraction,
member-entity maintenance, approval application, canvas/eval system entities, and
ACL-resource refreshes. **No general `skipHooks` flag** — connector writes to
project-defined types must run project hooks. And the TS-interface + lint chokepoint is
an *engineering* boundary, not a security one: the app DB credential can still issue SQL,
so critical invariants need DB backstops regardless.

**Fail closed on everything** (deny, throw, timeout, invalid output, oversized patch,
undeclared read, patch conflict, OOM, helper crash). A hook that denies everything is
valid configuration, not a fault. Recovery must not need a deploy and must not pass
through hooks: list versions, dry-run against fixtures, atomic rollback, disable binding,
activate with a version precondition, audited, owner-restricted.

**Open risks:** determinism (`Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in a hook), merge's ctx shape
(what is `candidate` for winner+losers?), blast radius of a hook that denies everything
and recovery without a deploy, and unmeasured per-write isolate cost.

Adversarial review of this design was dispatched to codex; if it completed, output is at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a/tasks/bjiinkahl.output`
(asks whether "bounded by construction" survives GC pauses, copy costs, host-callback
reentrancy; Postgres cost of longer transaction holds; funnel design; failure semantics).

Artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7cf74a93-2bf6-4106-a92f-b98c8702f890

===== reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules.md =====
---
name: reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules
description: "runMutationGate runs one undifferentiated interceptor list, so approval policy and data rules (period close, transition freeze) cannot be invoked separately — this is what blocks gating entity-merge"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-14T19:48:03.285Z
---

`runMutationGate` (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts`) folds
**approval policy** and **data rules** into one verdict over a single
`BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS` list. There is no way to say "approval is already
decided, run only the data-rule interceptors."

**What this blocks, concretely.** `entity-merge.ts` cannot be routed through the
gate, so period close and the transition freeze do not bind a merge. Proven by a
red test: with an invoice type closed through a date, merging a closed invoice as
the LOSER tombstones it, and merging into a closed WINNER rewrites its metadata —
both returned `success: true`.

The fix was implemented and reverted. Why it fails:
- every merge tombstones its loser, and
  `WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete` is `"approval"`
  (`src/authz/write-action-manifest.ts:64`), so gating merge as a `delete` makes
  the approval interceptor demand approval for **every** agent auto-merge under
  default policy;
- a merge transaction cannot express a defer — one atomic fuse plus an undo
  ledger, no post-commit hook;
- approval is already settled upstream: `handleMerge` runs
  `assessEntityResolution` and routes `review` to `proposeEntityMerge`, so
  reaching `applyMerge` means approval is decided. Re-asking double-gates.

**The unblock** is interceptor categories (`approval` vs `data-rule`) or a
`skipApprovalInterceptor` flag. That changes the gate's public contract, so
AGENTS.md requires a surfaced proposal first. It unblocks merge *and* every
future data-rule interceptor.

Recorded at the call site in a comment above `applyMerge` (commit `c27a77d9d`,
branch `feat/erp-period-close`) because the proving test was deleted with the
revert.

Related: the gate seam also cannot do **allocation** — it runs on a pool client
(`sql: getDb()`) in a different transaction from the INSERT, which is why gapless
numbering had to go inside `createEntity`'s `sql.begin`. See
[[reference_connectors_cannot_emit_entities]] for the other case where I reported
a gap from a bad grep instead of the tree.

===== reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes.md =====
---
name: reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes
description: "Resolving a rebase conflict with `git checkout --theirs` silently reverts bug fixes main landed inside the block your branch rewrote — find main's commits on that file since the merge-base and re-apply them, then mutation-verify with THEIR test"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:23:48.793Z
---

The mirror image of [[merge-main-conflict-resolution]]. That one warns that picking
**main's** side loses feature work. This is the other direction: picking the **branch's**
side loses bug fixes main landed while the branch was stale — and it is easier to miss,
because the branch side is "your" work and looks obviously correct.

**Concrete instance (2026-08-15, owletto#844 `feat/prodma-form`).** The branch extracted all
of `DynamicSchemaForm`'s inline field rendering into a `SchemaField` component, so a ~290-line
block became one `<SchemaField/>` call. Meanwhile owletto#828 had landed a fix *inside that
block*: a numeric JSON-Schema `enum` (`vat_rate: [0,1,10,20]`) crashed the whole entity page in
`formatLabel`, plus a round-trip bug writing `"20"` instead of `20`. Git reported one conflict
where main's side was the entire old block and the branch's side was EMPTY. Both naive
resolutions were wrong — main's drops the grid, the branch's reverts #828.

**The procedure that catches it:**
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..origin/main -- <conflicted-file>` — enumerate what main
   changed in that file. This is the step that turns an invisible loss into a checklist.
2. `git show <each-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply each fix into the branch's new structure
   (not the old one — the block may no longer exist).
3. **Mutation-verify with main's OWN test**, which survives the rebase untouched precisely
   because it is a different file. Revert your re-application → the test must go RED; restore
   → GREEN. Here `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` did exactly that. If main's fix
   had no test, write one before resolving.

`git checkout --theirs -- <file>` is still the right *starting* move when the branch
restructured the file (hand-deleting a 290-line conflict region gets blocked or botched), but
it is step one of three, never the resolution itself.

**Two traps hit while doing this:**
- `biome check --stdin-file-path=X < X` did NOT reproduce a lint error the same file reports
  on disk. A clean stdin probe is not evidence. Write the candidate content to a real path in
  the same directory and lint that instead.
- `biome check --write` reformatted a whole file (quote style + indentation) because owletto's
  committed files do not match its own biome config. That buries the real change in ~70 lines
  of noise. Revert the formatting, keep only the semantic hunk; the repo already carries 42
  pre-existing lint errors, so formatting is demonstrably not gated.

===== project_entity_write_hook_design.md =====
---
name: project_entity_write_hook_design
description: "Settled direction for ERP-style write rules: project-authored onWrite hooks run in an isolated-vm INSIDE the write transaction; core ships only funnel + hook + gapless-ordinal capability, zero domain vocabulary"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T00:41:16.853Z
---

Decided 2026-08-14/15. Supersedes the interceptor approach that was built and is
being DISCARDED (see [[project_erp_gap_branches_status]]).

**The model.** Project-authored hooks, co-located on the entity type, run in a V8
isolate INSIDE the write transaction:

```ts
const postingRules = (ctx) => {           // plain function — reuse across types
  if (ctx.op === "update" && FROZEN.has(ctx.current.status)) return ctx.deny("frozen");
};
defineEntityType({ key: "invoice", properties: {...}, onWrite: postingRules });
```

**Why transaction-local hooks work.** The historic objection to untrusted code in a
transaction is unbounded runtime pinning a connection. Running the hook after row locks
means **TOCTOU disappears** and the versioned-precondition / CAS scheme drafted earlier
is unnecessary. `isolated-vm` v6 (Node 22-24) / v7 aliased as `isolated-vm-next`
(Node 26+) already ship in `packages/server`; `run-script.ts` disposes the isolate to
terminate, uncatchable by the guest.

**CODEX REJECTED TWO PARTS OF THIS (2026-08-15) — do not rebuild on them:**
1. **No in-process tenant code in the gateway.** The gateway holds the transaction and
   locks; a **separate, credential-free executor process** runs the pure synchronous
   code. Failure path: kill and replace the helper, roll back.
2. **"Bounded by construction" is FALSE as stated.** A CPU budget does not bound
   wall-clock transaction hold time. Every phase needs its own deadline — cardinality,
   byte, queue, execution AND wall.
Verdict: "The transaction-local hook idea is no longer fundamentally wrong", but only
with those two corrections plus DB constraints as the final backstop, and hooks stay
disabled until the funnel has zero production bypasses.

**Core surface — three mechanisms, ZERO domain vocabulary.** No `lifecycle`,
`periodClose`, or `numbering` keys: those are core smuggling accounting back in as
config. Core provides only:
1. the write funnel,
2. the hook (locked `current` + normalized final `candidate` + `deny` + `patch` +
   a platform-prefetched declared read set),
3. a gapless-ordinal allocation capability the hook *requests* (allocation is the one
   thing a guest cannot be trusted to implement).

Shared implementations like a state-machine helper belong in a **project-level library
that compiles down to an onWrite** — "shared code" and "core code" are not the same
thing.

**Build order — the funnel FIRST.** A hook without a chokepoint is worse than nothing:
documented as an invariant while `entity-merge.ts`, `entity-link-upsert.ts`,
`classifier-extraction.ts` and `member-entity.ts` walk past it. Then approval/invariant
separation, then merge as a first-class op (not delete+update), then the hook.

**Authoring — do NOT co-locate a closure on the entity type.** I proposed
`defineEntityType({ onWrite: fn })`; codex rejected it and is right: `defineEntityType`
is intentionally a plain-data producer, and **a closure cannot be serialized** —
lexical bindings, imports and captured consts are not preserved by `Function#toString`.
Use a separate artifact with a FILE reference and data bindings:

```ts
defineEntityWriteHook({
  key: "ledger-write-rules",
  targets: [{ entityTypes: [invoice, payment, journalEntry],
              operations: ["create","update","delete","merge","unmerge"] }],
  reads: { period: entityByUniqueKey({ entityType: accountingPeriod,
             key: ["ledgerId","period"], lock: "share", maxRows: 1 }) },
  handler: writeHookFromFile("./hooks/ledger-write.ts"),
});
```
The type may reference the hook handle as optional sugar. The read-set DSL must expose
only indexed, statically bounded platform ops — never arbitrary SQL — each with max rows,
max bytes, lookup keys and lock mode; absence/set predicates must declare a coordination
strategy or be rejected at install. Install mirrors connectors + Behavior reaction files
(`desired-state.ts:943`). Persistence: immutable hook versions (source, artifact hash,
runtime ABI, declared capabilities), materialized active bindings keyed
`(org, entity_type, operation, order)`, atomic active-version pointer, disable+rollback.
Read bindings by index — never derive "latest" by scanning history.

**`unmerge` must be first-class too** — already implemented at `entity-merge.ts:450`;
hiding it behind update/delete recreates exactly the hole merge has now.

**More bypassers than previously recorded:** entity-link upsert, classifier extraction,
member-entity maintenance, approval application, canvas/eval system entities, and
ACL-resource refreshes. **No general `skipHooks` flag** — connector writes to
project-defined types must run project hooks. And the TS-interface + lint chokepoint is
an *engineering* boundary, not a security one: the app DB credential can still issue SQL,
so critical invariants need DB backstops regardless.

**Fail closed on everything** (deny, throw, timeout, invalid output, oversized patch,
undeclared read, patch conflict, OOM, helper crash). A hook that denies everything is
valid configuration, not a fault. Recovery must not need a deploy and must not pass
through hooks: list versions, dry-run against fixtures, atomic rollback, disable binding,
activate with a version precondition, audited, owner-restricted.

**Open risks:** determinism (`Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in a hook), merge's ctx shape
(what is `candidate` for winner+losers?), blast radius of a hook that denies everything
and recovery without a deploy, and unmeasured per-write isolate cost.

Adversarial review of this design was dispatched to codex; if it completed, output is at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a/tasks/bjiinkahl.output`
(asks whether "bounded by construction" survives GC pauses, copy costs, host-callback
reentrancy; Postgres cost of longer transaction holds; funnel design; failure semantics).

Artifact: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/7cf74a93-2bf6-4106-a92f-b98c8702f890

===== reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules.md =====
---
name: reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules
description: "runMutationGate runs one undifferentiated interceptor list, so approval policy and data rules (period close, transition freeze) cannot be invoked separately — this is what blocks gating entity-merge"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-14T19:48:03.285Z
---

`runMutationGate` (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts`) folds
**approval policy** and **data rules** into one verdict over a single
`BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS` list. There is no way to say "approval is already
decided, run only the data-rule interceptors."

**What this blocks, concretely.** `entity-merge.ts` cannot be routed through the
gate, so period close and the transition freeze do not bind a merge. Proven by a
red test: with an invoice type closed through a date, merging a closed invoice as
the LOSER tombstones it, and merging into a closed WINNER rewrites its metadata —
both returned `success: true`.

The fix was implemented and reverted. Why it fails:
- every merge tombstones its loser, and
  `WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete` is `"approval"`
  (`src/authz/write-action-manifest.ts:64`), so gating merge as a `delete` makes
  the approval interceptor demand approval for **every** agent auto-merge under
  default policy;
- a merge transaction cannot express a defer — one atomic fuse plus an undo
  ledger, no post-commit hook;
- approval is already settled upstream: `handleMerge` runs
  `assessEntityResolution` and routes `review` to `proposeEntityMerge`, so
  reaching `applyMerge` means approval is decided. Re-asking double-gates.

**The unblock** is interceptor categories (`approval` vs `data-rule`) or a
`skipApprovalInterceptor` flag. That changes the gate's public contract, so
AGENTS.md requires a surfaced proposal first. It unblocks merge *and* every
future data-rule interceptor.

Recorded at the call site in a comment above `applyMerge` (commit `c27a77d9d`,
branch `feat/erp-period-close`) because the proving test was deleted with the
revert.

Related: the gate seam also cannot do **allocation** — it runs on a pool client
(`sql: getDb()`) in a different transaction from the INSERT, which is why gapless
numbering had to go inside `createEntity`'s `sql.begin`. See
[[reference_connectors_cannot_emit_entities]] for the other case where I reported
a gap from a bad grep instead of the tree.

===== reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes.md =====
---
name: reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes
description: "Resolving a rebase conflict with `git checkout --theirs` silently reverts bug fixes main landed inside the block your branch rewrote — find main's commits on that file since the merge-base and re-apply them, then mutation-verify with THEIR test"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:23:48.793Z
---

The mirror image of [[merge-main-conflict-resolution]]. That one warns that picking
**main's** side loses feature work. This is the other direction: picking the **branch's**
side loses bug fixes main landed while the branch was stale — and it is easier to miss,
because the branch side is "your" work and looks obviously correct.

**Concrete instance (2026-08-15, owletto#844 `feat/prodma-form`).** The branch extracted all
of `DynamicSchemaForm`'s inline field rendering into a `SchemaField` component, so a ~290-line
block became one `<SchemaField/>` call. Meanwhile owletto#828 had landed a fix *inside that
block*: a numeric JSON-Schema `enum` (`vat_rate: [0,1,10,20]`) crashed the whole entity page in
`formatLabel`, plus a round-trip bug writing `"20"` instead of `20`. Git reported one conflict
where main's side was the entire old block and the branch's side was EMPTY. Both naive
resolutions were wrong — main's drops the grid, the branch's reverts #828.

**The procedure that catches it:**
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..origin/main -- <conflicted-file>` — enumerate what main
   changed in that file. This is the step that turns an invisible loss into a checklist.
2. `git show <each-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply each fix into the branch's new structure
   (not the old one — the block may no longer exist).
3. **Mutation-verify with main's OWN test**, which survives the rebase untouched precisely
   because it is a different file. Revert your re-application → the test must go RED; restore
   → GREEN. Here `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` did exactly that. If main's fix
   had no test, write one before resolving.

`git checkout --theirs -- <file>` is still the right *starting* move when the branch
restructured the file (hand-deleting a 290-line conflict region gets blocked or botched), but
it is step one of three, never the resolution itself.

**Two traps hit while doing this:**
- `biome check --stdin-file-path=X < X` did NOT reproduce a lint error the same file reports
  on disk. A clean stdin probe is not evidence. Write the candidate content to a real path in
  the same directory and lint that instead.
- `biome check --write` reformatted a whole file (quote style + indentation) because owletto's
  committed files do not match its own biome config. That buries the real change in ~70 lines
  of noise. Revert the formatting, keep only the semantic hunk; the repo already carries 42
  pre-existing lint errors, so formatting is demonstrably not gated.

===== project_entity_write_hook_design.md =====
---
name: project_entity_write_hook_design
description: "Settled direction for ERP-style write rules: project-authored onWrite hooks run in an isolated-vm INSIDE the write transaction; core ships only funnel + hook + gapless-ordinal capability, zero domain vocabulary"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T00:41:16.853Z
---

Decided 2026-08-14/15. Supersedes the interceptor approach that was built and is
being DISCARDED (see [[project_erp_gap_branches_status]]).

**The model.** Project-authored hooks, co-located on the entity type, run in a V8
isolate INSIDE the write transaction:

```ts
const postingRules = (ctx) => {           // plain function — reuse across types
  if (ctx.op === "update" && FROZEN.has(ctx.current.status)) return ctx.deny("frozen");
};
defineEntityType({ key: "invoice", properties: {...}, onWrite: postingRules });
```

**Why transaction-local hooks work.** The historic objection to untrusted code in a
transaction is unbounded runtime pinning a connection. Running the hook after row locks
means **TOCTOU disappears** and the versioned-precondition / CAS scheme drafted earlier
is unnecessary. `isolated-vm` v6 (Node 22-24) / v7 aliased as `isolated-vm-next`
(Node 26+) already ship in `packages/server`; `run-script.ts` disposes the isolate to
terminate, uncatchable by the guest.

**CODEX REJECTED TWO PARTS OF THIS (2026-08-15) — do not rebuild on them:**
1. **No in-process tenant code in the gateway.** The gateway holds the transaction and
   locks; a **separate, credential-free executor process** runs the pure synchronous
   code. Failure path: kill and replace the helper, roll back.
2. **"Bounded by construction" is FALSE as stated.** A CPU budget does not bound
   wall-clock transaction hold time. Every phase needs its own deadline — cardinality,
   byte, queue, execution AND wall.
Verdict: "The transaction-local hook idea is no longer fundamentally wrong", but only
with those two corrections plus DB constraints as the final backstop, and hooks stay
disabled until the funnel has zero production bypasses.

**Core surface — three mechanisms, ZERO domain vocabulary.** No `lifecycle`,
`periodClose`, or `numbering` keys: those are core smuggling accounting back in as
config. Core provides only:
1. the write funnel,
2. the hook (locked `current` + normalized final `candidate` + `deny` + `patch` +
   a platform-prefetched declared read set),
3. a gapless-ordinal allocation capability the hook *requests* (allocation is the one
   thing a guest cannot be trusted to implement).

Shared implementations like a state-machine helper belong in a **project-level library
that compiles down to an onWrite** — "shared code" and "core code" are not the same
thing.

**Build order — the funnel FIRST.** A hook without a chokepoint is worse than nothing:
documented as an invariant while `entity-merge.ts`, `entity-link-upsert.ts`,
`classifier-extraction.ts` and `member-entity.ts` walk past it. Then approval/invariant
separation, then merge as a first-class op (not delete+update), then the hook.

**Authoring — do NOT co-locate a closure on the entity type.** I proposed
`defineEntityType({ onWrite: fn })`; codex rejected it and is right: `defineEntityType`
is intentionally a plain-data producer, and **a closure cannot be serialized** —
lexical bindings, imports and captured consts are not preserved by `Function#toString`.
Use a separate artifact with a FILE reference and data bindings:

```ts
defineEntityWriteHook({
  key: "ledger-write-rules",
  targets: [{ entityTypes: [invoice, payment, journalEntry],
              operations: ["create","update","delete","merge","unmerge"] }],
  reads: { period: entityByUniqueKey({ entityType: accountingPeriod,
             key: ["ledgerId","period"], lock: "share", maxRows: 1 }) },
  handler: writeHookFromFile("./hooks/ledger-write.ts"),
});
```
The type may reference the hook handle as optional sugar. The read-set DSL must expose
only indexed, statically bounded platform ops — never arbitrary SQL — each with max rows,
max bytes, lookup keys and lock mode; absence/set predicates must declare a coordination
strategy or be rejected at install. Install mirrors connectors + Behavior reaction files
(`desired-state.ts:943`). Persistence: immutable hook versions (source, artifact hash,
runtime ABI, declared capabilities), materialized active bindings keyed
`(org, entity_type, operation, order)`, atomic active-version pointer, disable+rollback.
Read bindings by index — never derive "latest" by scanning history.

**`unmerge` must be first-class too** — already implemented at `entity-merge.ts:450`;
hiding it behind update/delete recreates exactly the hole merge has now.

**More bypassers than previously recorded:** entity-link upsert, classifier extraction,
member-entity maintenance, approval application, canvas/eval system entities, and
ACL-resource refreshes. **No general `skipHooks` flag** — connector writes to
project-defined types must run project hooks. And the TS-interface + lint chokepoint is
an *engineering* boundary, not a security one: the app DB credential can still issue SQL,
so critical invariants need DB backstops regardless.

**Fail closed on everything** (deny, throw, timeout, invalid output, oversized patch,
undeclared read, patch conflict, OOM, helper crash). A hook that denies everything is
valid configuration, not a fault. Recovery must not need a deploy and must not pass
through hooks: list versions, dry-run against fixtures, atomic rollback, disable binding,
activate with a version precondition, audited, owner-restricted.

**Open risks:** determinism (`Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in a hook), merge's ctx shape
(what is `candidate` for winner+losers?), blast radius of a hook that denies everything
and recovery without a deploy, and unmeasured per-write isolate cost.

Adversarial review of this design was dispatched to codex; if it completed, output is at
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-burakemre-Code-lobu/f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a/tasks/bjiinkahl.output`
(asks whether "bounded by construction" survives GC pauses, copy costs, host-callback
reentrancy; Postgres cost of longer transaction holds; funnel design; failure semantics).

===== reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules.md =====
---
name: reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules
description: "runMutationGate runs one undifferentiated interceptor list, so approval policy and data rules (period close, transition freeze) cannot be invoked separately — this is what blocks gating entity-merge"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-14T19:48:03.285Z
---

`runMutationGate` (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts`) folds
**approval policy** and **data rules** into one verdict over a single
`BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS` list. There is no way to say "approval is already
decided, run only the data-rule interceptors."

**What this blocks, concretely.** `entity-merge.ts` cannot be routed through the
gate, so period close and the transition freeze do not bind a merge. Proven by a
red test: with an invoice type closed through a date, merging a closed invoice as
the LOSER tombstones it, and merging into a closed WINNER rewrites its metadata —
both returned `success: true`.

The fix was implemented and reverted. Why it fails:
- every merge tombstones its loser, and
  `WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete` is `"approval"`
  (`src/authz/write-action-manifest.ts:64`), so gating merge as a `delete` makes
  the approval interceptor demand approval for **every** agent auto-merge under
  default policy;
- a merge transaction cannot express a defer — one atomic fuse plus an undo
  ledger, no post-commit hook;
- approval is already settled upstream: `handleMerge` runs
  `assessEntityResolution` and routes `review` to `proposeEntityMerge`, so
  reaching `applyMerge` means approval is decided. Re-asking double-gates.

**The unblock** is interceptor categories (`approval` vs `data-rule`) or a
`skipApprovalInterceptor` flag. That changes the gate's public contract, so
AGENTS.md requires a surfaced proposal first. It unblocks merge *and* every
future data-rule interceptor.

Recorded at the call site in a comment above `applyMerge` (commit `c27a77d9d`,
branch `feat/erp-period-close`) because the proving test was deleted with the
revert.

Related: the gate seam also cannot do **allocation** — it runs on a pool client
(`sql: getDb()`) in a different transaction from the INSERT, which is why gapless
numbering had to go inside `createEntity`'s `sql.begin`. See
[[reference_connectors_cannot_emit_entities]] for the other case where I reported
a gap from a bad grep instead of the tree.

===== reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes.md =====
---
name: reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes
description: "Resolving a rebase conflict with `git checkout --theirs` silently reverts bug fixes main landed inside the block your branch rewrote — find main's commits on that file since the merge-base and re-apply them, then mutation-verify with THEIR test"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:23:48.793Z
---

The mirror image of [[merge-main-conflict-resolution]]. That one warns that picking
**main's** side loses feature work. This is the other direction: picking the **branch's**
side loses bug fixes main landed while the branch was stale — and it is easier to miss,
because the branch side is "your" work and looks obviously correct.

**Concrete instance (2026-08-15, owletto#844 `feat/prodma-form`).** The branch extracted all
of `DynamicSchemaForm`'s inline field rendering into a `SchemaField` component, so a ~290-line
block became one `<SchemaField/>` call. Meanwhile owletto#828 had landed a fix *inside that
block*: a numeric JSON-Schema `enum` (`vat_rate: [0,1,10,20]`) crashed the whole entity page in
`formatLabel`, plus a round-trip bug writing `"20"` instead of `20`. Git reported one conflict
where main's side was the entire old block and the branch's side was EMPTY. Both naive
resolutions were wrong — main's drops the grid, the branch's reverts #828.

**The procedure that catches it:**
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..origin/main -- <conflicted-file>` — enumerate what main
   changed in that file. This is the step that turns an invisible loss into a checklist.
2. `git show <each-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply each fix into the branch's new structure
   (not the old one — the block may no longer exist).
3. **Mutation-verify with main's OWN test**, which survives the rebase untouched precisely
   because it is a different file. Revert your re-application → the test must go RED; restore
   → GREEN. Here `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` did exactly that. If main's fix
   had no test, write one before resolving.

`git checkout --theirs -- <file>` is still the right *starting* move when the branch
restructured the file (hand-deleting a 290-line conflict region gets blocked or botched), but
it is step one of three, never the resolution itself.

**Two traps hit while doing this:**
- `biome check --stdin-file-path=X < X` did NOT reproduce a lint error the same file reports
  on disk. A clean stdin probe is not evidence. Write the candidate content to a real path in
  the same directory and lint that instead.
- `biome check --write` reformatted a whole file (quote style + indentation) because owletto's
  committed files do not match its own biome config. That buries the real change in ~70 lines
  of noise. Revert the formatting, keep only the semantic hunk; the repo already carries 42
  pre-existing lint errors, so formatting is demonstrably not gated.

===== project_entity_write_hook_design.md =====
---
name: project_entity_write_hook_design
description: "Settled direction for ERP-style write rules: project-authored onWrite hooks run in an isolated-vm INSIDE the write transaction; core ships only funnel + hook + gapless-ordinal capability, zero domain vocabulary"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T00:41:16.853Z
---

Decided 2026-08-14/15. Supersedes the interceptor approach that was built and is
being DISCARDED (see [[project_erp_gap_branches_status]]).

**The model.** Project-authored hooks, co-located on the entity type, run in a V8
isolate INSIDE the write transaction:

```ts
const postingRules = (ctx) => {           // plain function — reuse across types
  if (ctx.op === "update" && FROZEN.has(ctx.current.status)) return ctx.deny("frozen");
};
defineEntityType({ key: "invoice", properties: {...}, onWrite: postingRules });
```

**Why transaction-local hooks work.** The historic objection to untrusted code in a
transaction is unbounded runtime pinning a connection. Running the hook after row locks
means **TOCTOU disappears** and the versioned-precondition / CAS scheme drafted earlier
is unnecessary. `isolated-vm` v6 (Node 22-24) / v7 aliased as `isolated-vm-next`
(Node 26+) already ship in `packages/server`; `run-script.ts` disposes the isolate to
terminate, uncatchable by the guest.

**CODEX REJECTED TWO PARTS OF THIS (2026-08-15) — do not rebuild on them:**
1. **No in-process tenant code in the gateway.** The gateway holds the transaction and
   locks; a **separate, credential-free executor process** runs the pure synchronous
   code. Failure path: kill and replace the helper, roll back.
2. **"Bounded by construction" is FALSE as stated.** A CPU budget does not bound
   wall-clock transaction hold time. Every phase needs its own deadline — cardinality,
   byte, queue, execution AND wall.
Verdict: "The transaction-local hook idea is no longer fundamentally wrong", but only
with those two corrections plus DB constraints as the final backstop, and hooks stay
disabled until the funnel has zero production bypasses.

**Core surface — three mechanisms, ZERO domain vocabulary.** No `lifecycle`,
`periodClose`, or `numbering` keys: those are core smuggling accounting back in as
config. Core provides only:
1. the write funnel,
2. the hook (locked `current` + normalized final `candidate` + `deny` + `patch` +
   a platform-prefetched declared read set),
3. a gapless-ordinal allocation capability the hook *requests* (allocation is the one
   thing a guest cannot be trusted to implement).

Shared implementations like a state-machine helper belong in a **project-level library
that compiles down to an onWrite** — "shared code" and "core code" are not the same
thing.

**Build order — the funnel FIRST.** A hook without a chokepoint is worse than nothing:
documented as an invariant while `entity-merge.ts`, `entity-link-upsert.ts`,
`classifier-extraction.ts` and `member-entity.ts` walk past it. Then approval/invariant
separation, then merge as a first-class op (not delete+update), then the hook.

**Authoring — do NOT co-locate a closure on the entity type.** I proposed
`defineEntityType({ onWrite: fn })`; codex rejected it and is right: `defineEntityType`
is intentionally a plain-data producer, and **a closure cannot be serialized** —
lexical bindings, imports and captured consts are not preserved by `Function#toString`.
Use a separate artifact with a FILE reference and data bindings:

```ts
defineEntityWriteHook({
  key: "ledger-write-rules",
  targets: [{ entityTypes: [invoice, payment, journalEntry],
              operations: ["create","update","delete","merge","unmerge"] }],
  reads: { period: entityByUniqueKey({ entityType: accountingPeriod,
             key: ["ledgerId","period"], lock: "share", maxRows: 1 }) },
  handler: writeHookFromFile("./hooks/ledger-write.ts"),
});
```
The type may reference the hook handle as optional sugar. The read-set DSL must expose
only indexed, statically bounded platform ops — never arbitrary SQL — each with max rows,
max bytes, lookup keys and lock mode; absence/set predicates must declare a coordination
strategy or be rejected at install. Install mirrors connectors + Behavior reaction files
(`desired-state.ts:943`). Persistence: immutable hook versions (source, artifact hash,
runtime ABI, declared capabilities), materialized active bindings keyed
`(org, entity_type, operation, order)`, atomic active-version pointer, disable+rollback.
Read bindings by index — never derive "latest" by scanning history.

**`unmerge` must be first-class too** — already implemented at `entity-merge.ts:450`;
hiding it behind update/delete recreates exactly the hole merge has now.

**More bypassers than previously recorded:** entity-link upsert, classifier extraction,
member-entity maintenance, approval application, canvas/eval system entities, and
ACL-resource refreshes. **No general `skipHooks` flag** — connector writes to
project-defined types must run project hooks. And the TS-interface + lint chokepoint is
an *engineering* boundary, not a security one: the app DB credential can still issue SQL,
so critical invariants need DB backstops regardless.

**Fail closed on everything** (deny, throw, timeout, invalid output, oversized patch,
undeclared read, patch conflict, OOM, helper crash). A hook that denies everything is
valid configuration, not a fault. Recovery must not need a deploy and must not pass
through hooks: list versions, dry-run against fixtures, atomic rollback, disable binding,
activate with a version precondition, audited, owner-restricted.

**Open risks:** determinism (`Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in a hook), merge's ctx shape
(what is `candidate` for winner+losers?), blast radius of a hook that denies everything
and recovery without a deploy, and unmeasured per-write isolate cost.

(asks whether "bounded by construction" survives GC pauses, copy costs, host-callback
reentrancy; Postgres cost of longer transaction holds; funnel design; failure semantics).

===== reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules.md =====
---
name: reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules
description: "runMutationGate runs one undifferentiated interceptor list, so approval policy and data rules (period close, transition freeze) cannot be invoked separately — this is what blocks gating entity-merge"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-14T19:48:03.285Z
---

`runMutationGate` (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts`) folds
**approval policy** and **data rules** into one verdict over a single
`BUILTIN_INTERCEPTORS` list. There is no way to say "approval is already
decided, run only the data-rule interceptors."

**What this blocks, concretely.** `entity-merge.ts` cannot be routed through the
gate, so period close and the transition freeze do not bind a merge. Proven by a
red test: with an invoice type closed through a date, merging a closed invoice as
the LOSER tombstones it, and merging into a closed WINNER rewrites its metadata —
both returned `success: true`.

The fix was implemented and reverted. Why it fails:
- every merge tombstones its loser, and
  `WRITE_ACTION_MANIFEST.entity.defaultEffect.delete` is `"approval"`
  (`src/authz/write-action-manifest.ts:64`), so gating merge as a `delete` makes
  the approval interceptor demand approval for **every** agent auto-merge under
  default policy;
- a merge transaction cannot express a defer — one atomic fuse plus an undo
  ledger, no post-commit hook;
- approval is already settled upstream: `handleMerge` runs
  `assessEntityResolution` and routes `review` to `proposeEntityMerge`, so
  reaching `applyMerge` means approval is decided. Re-asking double-gates.

**The unblock** is interceptor categories (`approval` vs `data-rule`) or a
`skipApprovalInterceptor` flag. That changes the gate's public contract, so
AGENTS.md requires a surfaced proposal first. It unblocks merge *and* every
future data-rule interceptor.

Recorded at the call site in a comment above `applyMerge` (commit `c27a77d9d`,
branch `feat/erp-period-close`) because the proving test was deleted with the
revert.

Related: the gate seam also cannot do **allocation** — it runs on a pool client
(`sql: getDb()`) in a different transaction from the INSERT, which is why gapless
numbering had to go inside `createEntity`'s `sql.begin`. See
[[reference_connectors_cannot_emit_entities]] for the other case where I reported
a gap from a bad grep instead of the tree.

===== reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes.md =====
---
name: reference_taking_the_branch_side_reverts_merged_fixes
description: "Resolving a rebase conflict with `git checkout --theirs` silently reverts bug fixes main landed inside the block your branch rewrote — find main's commits on that file since the merge-base and re-apply them, then mutation-verify with THEIR test"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T02:23:48.793Z
---

The mirror image of [[merge-main-conflict-resolution]]. That one warns that picking
**main's** side loses feature work. This is the other direction: picking the **branch's**
side loses bug fixes main landed while the branch was stale — and it is easier to miss,
because the branch side is "your" work and looks obviously correct.

**Concrete instance (2026-08-15, owletto#844 `feat/prodma-form`).** The branch extracted all
of `DynamicSchemaForm`'s inline field rendering into a `SchemaField` component, so a ~290-line
block became one `<SchemaField/>` call. Meanwhile owletto#828 had landed a fix *inside that
block*: a numeric JSON-Schema `enum` (`vat_rate: [0,1,10,20]`) crashed the whole entity page in
`formatLabel`, plus a round-trip bug writing `"20"` instead of `20`. Git reported one conflict
where main's side was the entire old block and the branch's side was EMPTY. Both naive
resolutions were wrong — main's drops the grid, the branch's reverts #828.

**The procedure that catches it:**
1. `git log --oneline <merge-base>..origin/main -- <conflicted-file>` — enumerate what main
   changed in that file. This is the step that turns an invisible loss into a checklist.
2. `git show <each-commit> -- <file>` and re-apply each fix into the branch's new structure
   (not the old one — the block may no longer exist).
3. **Mutation-verify with main's OWN test**, which survives the rebase untouched precisely
   because it is a different file. Revert your re-application → the test must go RED; restore
   → GREEN. Here `dynamic-schema-form.numeric-enum.test.tsx` did exactly that. If main's fix
   had no test, write one before resolving.

`git checkout --theirs -- <file>` is still the right *starting* move when the branch
restructured the file (hand-deleting a 290-line conflict region gets blocked or botched), but
it is step one of three, never the resolution itself.

**Two traps hit while doing this:**
- `biome check --stdin-file-path=X < X` did NOT reproduce a lint error the same file reports
  on disk. A clean stdin probe is not evidence. Write the candidate content to a real path in
  the same directory and lint that instead.
- `biome check --write` reformatted a whole file (quote style + indentation) because owletto's
  committed files do not match its own biome config. That buries the real change in ~70 lines
  of noise. Revert the formatting, keep only the semantic hunk; the repo already carries 42
  pre-existing lint errors, so formatting is demonstrably not gated.

===== reference_entity_change_history_already_exists.md =====
---
name: reference_entity_change_history_already_exists
description: "Lobu DOES record field-level entity change history via recordChangeEvent — I wrongly claimed it didn't by grepping for literal `INSERT INTO events` inside manage_entity.ts"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-13T21:33:26.987Z
---

`manage_entity.ts:547` (handleUpdate) calls `recordChangeEvent` with a **real field-level diff**:
`metadata.changes = [{field, old, new}]`, plus `createdBy`, `clientId`, `entityIds`, landing in
`events` with `semantic_type='change'` (indexed by `idx_events_entity_ids`).

A whole audit family exists in `utils/insert-event.ts`: `recordChangeEvent`,
`recordConfigChangeEvent`, `recordWorkspaceChangeEvent`, `recordLifecycleEvent`, all routed through
`insertConnectionlessAuditEvent`, which enforces idempotency via a reserved
`metadata._lobu_idempotency_key` + `idx_events_org_idempotency_key`.

**The trap that produced a wrong finding:** I grepped `manage_entity.ts` for `INSERT INTO events`,
found nothing, and reported "writes NO event and NO audit row". The write goes through a *helper*.
Grepping for raw SQL inside a call site proves nothing about whether a write happens — grep for the
**concept** (`audit`, `recordChange`, `Event(`) or trace the imports. Same class as
[[feedback_absence_needs_origin_main_grep]]: absence needs the right probe, not just a probe.

**Real gaps (verified, narrower than my claim):**
- Only `handleUpdate` records. `handleCreate`, `handleDelete`, `handleLink`, `handleUnlink`,
  `handleMerge`, `handleUnmerge`, `handleUpdateLink` record nothing.
- `recordChangeEvent` is **fire-and-forget** — never throws, retries twice, then logs ERROR and
  DROPS the row. Not acceptable as a legal audit trail.
- It runs **post-commit**, outside `updateEntity`'s transaction (`entity-management.ts:616`).
- `content` diffs are redacted to the literal string `"[changed]"`.
- Coverage is safe on one axis: `updateEntity` has exactly ONE caller (manage_entity.ts:480), and
  the sandbox `client.entities.*` routes through manage_entity actions — so there is no unaudited
  side door.

[[reference_events_metadata_watcher_id_means_about_not_produced]]

===== reference_write_gate_is_the_only_non_agent_authorable_layer.md =====
---
name: reference_write_gate_is_the_only_non_agent_authorable_layer
description: "Every declarative layer in Lobu is agent-writable at runtime via manage_entity_schema — the entity mutation gate is the sole exception, and that asymmetry is the real extensibility gap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-13T23:38:44.116Z
---

`manage_entity_schema` writes `metadata_schema`, `event_kinds`, `backing_sql`, `backing_source`,
`metrics_config`, `current_view_template_version_id` — **all at runtime, no deploy**. An agent can
define a type's schema, its event vocabulary, a derived SQL view, a metric contract, and its UI
template by itself.

**The write gate is the one layer it cannot touch.**
`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts` is a genuine interceptor pipeline in front of
every user-facing entity write (create/update/delete + Behavior window promotion). Outcomes:
`allow` / `deny` (hard, no approval queued) / `defer` (queue a durable approval, executed strictly
POST-COMMIT). For updates the decision is per-FIELD — interceptors return `requireApproval` sets
that UNION, and reserved `$name` / `$parent_id` / `$content` paths let field rules cover attributes.

But `registerMutationInterceptor` (:186) is a compile-time TS call, and **outside tests it is never
called** — production ships exactly one interceptor (`approvalInterceptor`). No connector, Behavior,
or sandbox script can register one; the sandbox couldn't host it anyway (`client.query` forces
`SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, and the gate runs inside the caller's tx).

**Second constraint:** the gate is a no-op for humans.
`entity-policy.ts:796` `if (args.principalKind === "user") return "allow";` — same short-circuit at
:883, :916, :976. Comment: "Human edits are never gated here — role restrictions for humans live in
the tool-access tier." So any data-dependent rule (frozen document, legal state transition, debit=credit)
binds AGENTS but not people.

**Design conclusion for data-dependent rules** (freeze / state machine / balanced entry): make the
RULE data on the entity type (agent-authored, like `metrics_config` already is) and keep ENFORCEMENT
deterministic in ONE interceptor that reads it. Not "agent decides at write time" — an LLM in the
write path is nondeterministic, costly, arguable, and binds only that agent, never the import script
or the second human. See [[feedback_put_the_check_at_the_chokepoint]].

**Why a state machine is not a workaround for permissions:** a permission answers "may this principal
write this field" (principal + resource + field); a transition rule answers "may this value become
that value" (current data + proposed data). The second strictly needs row data, so no principal-only
permission system can express "posted invoices are immutable" — same principal, different data.
Lobu already half-accepts this: `entity_approval_policies.entity_id` scopes a rule to ONE row and
`entities.field_controls` to one field of one row.

**DO NOT "open" the user short-circuit — it is LOAD-BEARING.** `evaluateEntityFieldUpdates`
(entity-policy.ts:1000-1007) makes any human-owned field `require_approval` *unconditionally*; that
only works because the caller is never human. Route human updates through it and every human edit of
a field a human previously set queues an approval card **to themselves**. `affirm_fields`
(entity-management.ts:596) and the approval-apply path writing `source:"human"` share the same
premise. Correct shape: call `runMutationGate` for human edits (today the whole gate call is skipped
for them — `entity-management.ts:654` wraps it in `if (!isHumanEdit)`, so entity-policy.ts:796 is
NEVER REACHED on updates) and add the data-dependent rule as a *separate interceptor* that denies
regardless of `principalKind`. The pipeline already folds several (entity-mutation-gate.ts:241-260).

**The gate has a second door:** `applyEntityFieldChangeProposal`
(tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts:1085) writes via `mergeEntityFields` with NO `runMutationGate`.
A proposal queued pre-freeze and approved post-freeze writes into a frozen row. Any freeze must be
enforced at the write chokepoint (inside the tx / `mergeEntityFields`), not only in the pipeline.

**Field ownership is per TOP-LEVEL metadata key** (`entity-management.ts:684-694`). Storing document
lines as one `lines` array makes the whole array a single ownership atom: once a human edits any
line, every later agent-attributed write to `lines` is forced to approval. Inline recompute inside
the human's own save is fine (`isHumanEdit` true); a *background* agent recompute is blocked.

**The RULE needs no new column or table.** `entity_types.metadata_schema` is typed
`Record<string, Unknown>` on the tool contract (contracts/tools/manage-entity-schema.ts:85) and the
server AJV runs `strict: false` (ajv-singleton.ts:27), so unknown `x-` keywords survive a
write/read round trip. Shipped precedent: `x-link-entity-type` is resolved server-side
(manage_entity.ts:1146) AND read by Owletto (entity-table-view.tsx:201). So a transition/freeze rule
is just `x-transitions` on the schema — agent-authorable via `manage_entity_schema` at runtime, and
that tool's create/update is itself approval-queued, so an agent can't silently remove its own rule.
Do NOT propose a rules table.

**Entity concurrency is FIELD-grained and the server is already correct** — do NOT propose a row
version (`xmin`, a `_version` column, `updated_at` CAS). `updateEntity` reads the row `FOR UPDATE`
*inside* the tx (entity-management.ts:616) and `computeFieldMerge` merges incoming keys into that
locked read (:728), so concurrent edits to DIFFERENT fields both land. A row token would reject
exactly those — the common case — trading a rare silent overwrite for frequent false conflicts.
**The real lost-update bug is in the CLIENT:** `entity-tabs/index.tsx:105` sends
`metadata: metadataDirty ? metadata : undefined` — one dirty flag for the WHOLE object, so every
save carries the sender's stale copy of every other field. Fix = send only changed keys (one
frontend file, zero server change). If same-field conflict detection is ever wanted,
`field_controls.set_at` (entity-field-merge.ts:22) is already a per-field token.

Related: [[project_prodma_erp_to_lobu_poc]], [[reference_entity_change_history_already_exists]],
[[project_authz_foundation_program]], [[project_write_gate_generalization]]

===== reference_metric_design_answers_aggregates_with_an_ops_toggle.md =====
---
name: reference_metric_design_answers_aggregates_with_an_ops_toggle
description: docs/plans/define-metric-design.md (shipped 2026-07-15) already decides how aggregates scale — derived backing_sql entity + materialize-when-slow; do NOT propose write-time rollups
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-13T23:38:52.218Z
---

`docs/plans/define-metric-design.md` (564 lines, **Status: Shipped (v1) 2026-07-15**) is the
authority on aggregates. Two load-bearing decisions:

- **"Everything lowers to a `backing`-SQL derived entity"** — `eventSets`/`measures`/`segments` are
  authoring sugar the compiler lowers into `entity_types.backing_sql`. No parallel engine.
- **":41 / :494 — "Materialization is an operational toggle (plain view → materialized view when
  slow), not a concept"** — it changes *latency*, not *coverage*. The microbatch/partial/final
  engine was **explicitly cut** (v5) and survives only as a deferred appendix (:560).

**Do not propose write-time rollups for aggregates.** I did in an earlier round, reasoning from the
AGENTS.md "request paths never aggregate history" invariant — but that invariant names the
append-only *history* tables (`events`, `agent_transcript_snapshot`, `session_calls`), and the metric
design already rejected the counter approach. Proposing it re-litigates a settled decision.

**Choosing the instrument:** an aggregate over `events` → `metrics_config`. An aggregate over
*entity rows* (invoice totals, customer balance) → a derived type with `backing_sql`. The compiler is
`FROM events` + `eventSet.by:"alias"` + `reads:"current"` ONLY; cross-entity joins, window/link
resolvers and raw/asOf reads throw NotImplemented (compiler.ts:14-15).

**The real, much smaller gap:** the toggle is documented but never exercised — **zero
`CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` anywhere in `packages/` or `db/`** (the `WITH x AS MATERIALIZED` hits are
CTE hints, unrelated) and nothing schedules a refresh. Measure before building against it.

**The doc is current, not stale** (checked 2026-08-14): `metrics/compiler.ts` last changed
substantively 2026-06-16; everything touching `packages/server/src/metrics/` since is incidental
(workspace-audit exclusion, per-user visibility). Un-revisited ≠ out of date.

**If a read ever does need to be fast, the codebase's own habit is a write-time materialized
COLUMN, not a matview** — `manage_behaviors/list.ts:59` (completion stamp),
`utils/table-schema.ts:510`, materialized MCP activity identities. Two months of the doc's
matview instruction sitting unused vs repeated write-time columns: precedent breaks the tie.

Related: [[project_prodma_erp_to_lobu_poc]], [[feedback_check_prior_sessions_before_designing]],
[[reference_write_gate_is_the_only_non_agent_authorable_layer]]

===== project_entity_write_path_has_no_identity_contract.md =====
---
name: project_entity_write_path_has_no_identity_contract
description: "Connectors normalize identities correctly via the SDK contract; run_sdk/createEntity have no identity contract at all, which is how 92% of buremba's resolvable identifiers ended up as raw metadata strings"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c3dc213c-a275-44a5-9345-8bf68a35760f
  modified: 2026-07-30T01:16:40.319Z
---

**Connectors are not the problem — the non-connector write path is.** Traced 2026-07-29 in prod org `buremba` (`8dc12bdd-5d8c-4768-a2e9-a18005cc5ebd`).

**The SDK contract exists and connectors honour it.** `packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-normalize.ts` exports `normalizePhone` / `normalizeEmail` / `normalizeEmailDomain` / `normalizeAuthUserId` / `normalizeIdentifier` over an identity-namespace registry, and documents the design decision explicitly: "Connectors should pass in values that already represent a specific E.164 number. The normalizer's job is cleanup (spaces, dashes, parens, `+`), **not country-code guessing**." WhatsApp obeyed — it wrote `905395102240` into `entity_identities` with a namespace and `source_connector`. **Do not propose a workspace-default-region / country-code inference feature; the contract deliberately rejects it and the importer is where the region knowledge actually lives.**

**The bad data never met a connector.** The 07-06 address-book import was `run_sdk`: 26 `run_sdk completed` audit events spanning 21:44:00→21:45:36 bracket 541 person entities created 21:45:10→21:45:16 with metadata keys `aliases, email, first_name, last_name, phone`. Only 3 of 541 got an `entity_identities` row. No entity-creating run row exists (the only runs in that window are `chrome` browser actions), no `connector_key` on any related event, `created_by` is a user id. Same shape for the LinkedIn batches (18:59 / 19:02 / 21:19, keys `company, email, first_name, last_name, linkedin_url`) and the Instagram/X batch on 07-08.

**Scale of the split** — live persons in `buremba`, `deleted_at is null and merged_into is null`:

```
persons  meta_phone  meta_email  ident_phone  ident_email
   4358         534         535           18           69
```

1069 identifiers in `metadata` against 87 identity claims. ~92% of the workspace's resolvable identity carries no namespace, no provenance, no normalization, and no uniqueness — and was not matchable at all until #2152 taught the matcher to read metadata defensively. `packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts` has **zero** `entity_identities` references, so `createEntity` cannot resolve identity even in principle.

**Consequence.** `053-559-51101` (Turkish local) and `905355951101@s.whatsapp.net` are the same number in two formats on two entities. Deterministic rules can't join them, so they surface as a human approval — paying human attention for a plumbing bug. Under the SDK contract the honest outcome is that a non-E.164 value never becomes an identity claim at all: it stays a display string until the source data is fixed.

**Fix direction (not built):** `run_sdk`/`createEntity` accept identity claims and run them through `normalizeIdentifier`, so collisions happen at write time. "Fozkan" would then have hit the April WhatsApp shell as it was created — no proposal, no queue, no fingerprint to go stale. Backfilling the 534 metadata-only phones is downstream of that and only worth doing once the writer stops producing more.

**It is a MISSING CAPABILITY, not a bypass (verified 2026-07-29 against the working tree).** `packages/core/src/contracts/tools/manage-entity.ts` has no identity parameter on create or update at all — its only `identit*` hits are merge/unmerge prose and `merge_evidence.identity_ids`, which is provenance for a merge, not a write. `manage_entity.ts` imports only `loadLiveEntityIdentities` (read). So an agent can create a person and has literally no way to say "this phone is an identity claim" — metadata is the only slot that exists. Per [[feedback_generalize_fix_then_grep_class]] the fix is to add the capability, not to infer identities from metadata after the fact.

**There is no chokepoint to add it to.** Seven independent `INSERT INTO entity_identities` sites: `tools/save_content.ts:326`, `auth/subject-identities.ts:60` and `:107`, `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512`, `utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424`, `utils/canvas-events.ts:161`, `utils/member-entity.ts:136`. Any identity contract has to land as a shared writer these seven adopt, or it will be an eighth dialect.

**The storage question comes first.** Prod `entity_identities` is 11 columns: `id, organization_id, entity_id, namespace, identifier, source_connector, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, merged_from_entity_id, connection_id`. `ConnectorFact` carries `assurance`, `providerStableId`, `sourceAccountId`, `validTo` and `normalizedValue` — **all five are discarded at the write boundary**. Two open decisions before any code: (1) which of those become columns; (2) `identifier` uniqueness is on normalized *spelling*, not canonical value, so `05355951101` and `905355951101` both satisfy `idx_entity_identities_live_unique` — a correct identity write still would not collide. Also note `providerStableId`/`sourceAccountId` are required on `ConnectorFact`, which is exactly what makes the contract unusable for a non-connector writer and guarantees the bypass.

**Measured cost of the storage gap, 2026-07-30.** Of the 16 merge approvals still pending in `buremba`, exactly **4** (runs 702088, 702091, 702092, 702094) yield **zero** evidence and therefore cannot be healed in one click — in every case the winner holds a national-format `metadata.phone` (`05067888845`) against a loser identity row `905067888845`. The other 12 match on exact digits and heal on one Confirm. That 4/16 is the concrete price of decision (2) above: **it is the missing canonical-value column, not a missing normalizer.** Adding country-code inference to `normalizeScalar` would "fix" all four and is the wrong fix — the contract rejects guessing, and the region knowledge lives in the importer. A canonical-value column populated at write time by the importer that knows the region is the fix that does not require guessing later.

## Diagnosis of `entity_identities` itself (2026-07-30) — the table is sound, its uniqueness rule serves the wrong half

**Deleting it is not an option: it is the authz substrate.** `packages/server/src/authz/member-claim-predicate.ts` calls itself "the single source of truth for does this (org, user) resolve to a live `$member`" and answers it through one `entity_identities` row with `namespace='auth_user_id'`. `channel-visibility.ts`, `channel-messages-visibility.ts`, `resource-visibility.ts`, `access-graph.ts`, `channel-entity.ts`, `channel-about.ts` and `auth/subject-identities.ts` all join it. Any "should we just drop it?" question is really about the phone/email rows only.

**Prod splits into two populations wanting opposite rules** (live rows, all orgs): opaque provider IDs — `linkedin_slug` 2626, `github_user_id` 1116, `github_login` 1093, `x_user_id` 736, `x_handle` 557, `ig_username` 499, `wa_jid` 357, `watcher_key` 165, `auth_user_id` 45, `slack_user_id` 25, `domain` 19, `slack_channel_id` 11 — where spelling **is** the identity and exact match is correct (~7,200 rows, working fine); versus human-entered contact identifiers `phone` 357 + `email` 105 (462 rows), where spelling is an accident of the typist. Only the second group is broken.

**`uniquePerOrg` is declared and never read.** `packages/connector-sdk/src/identity-namespaces.ts` defines `uniquePerOrg: boolean` ("true means a value should identify at most one entity per org") and sets it false on `email_domain` with a note that many people share a domain. Verified on `origin/main`: the identifier's ONLY occurrences are its own declarations — no consumer. Meanwhile the DB enforces one blanket `UNIQUE (organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` over every namespace. Declared semantics and enforced semantics are disconnected; the knob that would fix this already exists and is inert.

**CORRECTION (same day, before building): the paragraph below OVERSTATES the silent-skip bug — I read `insertIdentities` without reading its caller.** `lookupMatches` (`utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:332`) resolves every incoming `(namespace, identifier)` to its owning entity *before* any insert, so in the common same-spelling case the connector path finds the existing owner and attaches to it: no duplicate created, no evidence lost. The ON CONFLICT skip is deliberate and documented at line 785 ("an identifier that ON CONFLICT-skipped because another entity already owns it stays with that entity, so the map must not mis-claim it"). What survives as real is narrow: (a) the `catch` → `return []` swallows genuine DB errors into a success shape, a fail-closed violation; (b) the contested drop has no log in the one-sided case, even though line 772 already warns for the *ambiguous* case. Neither justifies a redesign. **Lesson: read the caller before calling a guarded skip a silent bug** — [[feedback_gateway_predicate_cannot_replace_worker_state]] is the same shape of mistake.

**Also DROPPED: my "assurance-gated uniqueness" design was solving a problem the policy declines to have.** `entity-resolution/policy.ts:19` defines `ResolutionDecision = "auto_merge" | "review"`, and every rule in `DEFAULT_PERSON_RESOLUTION_RULES` is **`review`** — email and phone both. So no uniqueness mechanism (canonical column, assurance column, threshold index) would have prevented the 18 approvals: the shipped policy asks for review on contact-identifier matches on purpose, because a shared phone is not proof. The 18 were the system working as designed; the only bug was the fingerprint. `onMatch` in `x-lobu-resolution` is already the knob if auto-merge is ever wanted — configuration, not a migration. Do not re-propose assurance-gated uniqueness without first re-reading those default rules.

**The perverse part (OVERSTATED — see correction above): the unique index destroys the evidence of sameness in BOTH directions.** `insertIdentities` (`utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:512`) does `ON CONFLICT (organization_id, namespace, identifier) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL DO UPDATE … WHERE entity_identities.entity_id = EXCLUDED.entity_id`, so a claim already held by a *different* entity is **silently skipped** — no exception, omitted from `RETURNING`, and the sole caller uses the result only to seed `metadata.aliases`, so the dropped identifier does not even become an alias. Therefore:
- **Same spelling** → conflict → second entity silently keeps **no** claim → the identical identifier that proved they were the same is now recorded on only one side, so identity-based matching cannot see it.
- **Different spelling** → no conflict → both keep claims → no match anyway.

Either way the identity layer fails to prove sameness, and the duplicate survives looking identity-less. That is the same end state as the `run_sdk` metadata-only shape, reached by a completely different route — so "silently drop" is the *current* collision behavior at the write layer; the review card comes later from the resolution/proposal path, not from here. The surrounding `try/catch` also returns `[]` on any error with only a `warn`, which reinterprets a failed durable identity write as "nothing to attach" — worth checking against the repo's fail-closed invariant.

**Interview put to the user 2026-07-30 (unanswered, re-ask before building):** (1) is phone/email an identity or an attribute — drop them as claims and keep them as resolution inputs, add a canonical-value column, split email-vs-phone, or make `uniquePerOrg` load-bearing per namespace; (2) on collision — queue review, auto-merge deterministic exact matches, or reject the write; (3) the 1069 existing metadata identifiers — forward-only, backfill+auto-merge, or backfill+queue; (4) scope — design doc first, write path only, both together, or park it. **Do not start building until these are answered**; the options diverge on whether 462 rows get deleted or gain a column.

Related: [[project_merge_evidence_checkable_vs_uncheckable]], [[project_merge_fingerprint_stranding]].

===== reference_entity_gate_transaction_context_is_inconsistent.md =====
---
name: reference_entity_gate_transaction_context_is_inconsistent
description: "runMutationGate gets a POOL client on create/delete but the write TRANSACTION on update and Behavior promotion — 'the gate runs outside the transaction' is false and cost a whole design"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f0b3eac6-8946-4c9e-bbf8-24d856a5592a
  modified: 2026-08-15T00:39:15.723Z
---

The entity mutation gate does **not** have a consistent transaction context:

- **create / delete** — `manage_entity.ts:320` (and 3 other sites) pass `sql: getDb()`,
  a **pool client**. `createEntity` then opens its own `sql.begin`. Different transaction.
- **update** — `entity-management.ts` opens `sql.begin` and passes `sql: tx` into
  `runMutationGate`. **Same transaction as the write.**
- **Behavior promotion** — `promote-keyed-entities.ts` also passes `tx`.

**Why this matters.** I asserted repeatedly that "the gate runs on a pool client in a
different transaction from the write" and built a design on it — project code is safe at
the gate because it cannot hold a transaction open. That is true only for create/delete,
and update is where document rules do most of their work. Caught by an adversarial codex
review, then verified directly.

Two consequences that survive:
- **Gapless numbering must allocate inside `createEntity`'s `sql.begin`.** The create
  gate really is a pool client, so allocating there commits early and is burned on
  rollback. Proven by mutation test: swapping `tx` for the pool client reddens exactly
  one case, the rollback one — the concurrency test stays green, because contiguity alone
  cannot see the gap.
- **"The gate runs outside the transaction" would be a NEW contract to establish**, not a
  property to rely on.

Also from that review: splitting write rules by refuse-vs-mutate is a **false dichotomy**.
A refusal can depend on transactional state — two requests both read `draft`, one sets
`posted`, the other changes the amount, and you get a posted invoice whose amount changed
after posting. The useful classification is by state dependency: proposal-local /
current-row / mutable-config / cross-row / write-transforming. Existence constraints
("one open stocktake per warehouse") fit none of them and need a **partial unique index**,
not a rule.

Related: [[project_entity_write_hook_design]] ·
[[reference_mutation_gate_folds_approval_and_data_rules]]

Verified on origin/main 2026-08-15: `entity-mutation-gate.ts` contains **zero** occurrences of
