# UI surface audit — `packages/owletto`

**One-line answer.** Lobu's UI is NOT "441 screens = 441 hand-built React files". There is a real, working schema-driven renderer: a JSON-Schema stored per user-defined entity type drives the list (table/board/gallery), the detail page, and the edit form for free. What is missing is the ERP **depth** of that renderer: the form and grid are flat-scalar only, and none of the transactional ergonomics (keyboard grid entry, master-detail lines, lookups, saved views, per-field filters, unsaved guards) or document outputs (PDF/Excel) exist. Feasible in kind; HARD in completeness.

Scope caveat: I read real code + the `entity_types`/`entities` schema evidence on the server side only where it proves what the frontend renders. Everything cited is in `packages/owletto` unless marked `(server)`.

---

## 1. What the frontend actually renders — route map

File-based routing (TanStack Router); all routes in `src/routeTree.gen.ts`, route files under `src/app/` (61 route `.tsx` files).

- Public/auth: `/` landing, `/auth/*` (login, callback, accept-invitation, reset-password), `/oauth/*`, `/orgs/new`, `/slack/claim` — `src/app/auth/login.tsx`, `src/app/index.tsx`.
- Workspace shell `/$owner` (`src/app/$owner.tsx`) with static nav sections, `src/lib/owner-sections.ts:28`: Activity, Connectors, Agents, Behaviors, Memory, Settings.
- Bespoke product screens (hand-built): `/$owner/connectors/*`, `/$owner/agents/*` (incl. guardrails/skills/permissions/identity/models), `/$owner/behaviors/*`, `/$owner/events`, `/$owner/settings/organization`, `/$owner/entity-types/$slug` (type admin), deployments, members.
- **Schema-driven screens:** `/$owner/memory` hub (`src/app/$owner/memory/*`), the first-class type list `/$owner/<type>` (`src/app/$owner/$entityType/index.tsx:12`), and entity detail `/$owner/<type>/<slug>` resolved through the catch-all `/$owner/$` (`src/app/$owner/$.tsx:45`).

So the UI is two populations: ~10 hand-built Lobu-product sections, and one generic "Memory" surface that renders *any* entity type.

## 2. Generic, schema-driven components — the decisive question

**YES.** An entity type carries a `metadata_schema` (JSON-Schema); the UI renders it generically end-to-end.

- **List/grid** — `EntityTypeListPanel` (`src/components/entities/entity-type-list-panel.tsx:80`) feeds `EntityTableView` (`src/components/entities/entity-table-view.tsx:173`). Columns are *derived from the schema*: each `properties[k]` with `"x-table-column": true` becomes a sortable column (`entity-table-view.tsx:215-309`), formatted by annotation (`x-currency`, `format: date|uri`, `enum`, `x-link-entity-type` cross-links, `x-table-label`) via `resolveColumnFormat` (`entity-table-view.tsx:123`). Also derives parent/relationship/derived-measure columns (`entity-table-view.tsx:355-521`).
- **Alternate list views** — board (Kanban, drag-to-update) `src/components/entities/entity-board-view.tsx`; gallery expressed in pure template DSL `src/components/entities/entity-view-templates.ts:60`. All three are wired through the JSON→UI interpreter.
- **Form** — `DynamicSchemaForm` (`src/components/dynamic-schema-form.tsx:146`) renders text / number / boolean / enum-select / string-array inputs from the schema (incl. `required`, `readOnly`, `description` as label). Used for create (`src/components/create-entity-form.tsx:156`) and edit (`src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx:167`).
- **Detail page** — `EntityTabsContent` (`src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx:324`): read-only Overview (a `JsonRenderer` dashboard), relationships list, and the edit sidebar. `src/app/$owner/$.tsx:102` resolves the entity generically.
- **JSON→UI interpreter + plugin registry** — `JsonRenderer` (`src/lib/json-renderer/renderer.tsx`) interprets `{type, children, props}` trees with data bindings, `if`/`each` control flow, charts, tables, and app-registered nodes (`entity-table`, `entity-board`, `entity-link`, `entity-avatar`, `metric-series`) at `src/components/entities/renderer-registry.tsx:144`. Types may ship **authored type-level templates** (`view_templates` on the type, `src/lib/api/entities.ts:267`) and per-entity dashboard tabs (`entity.json_template`, rendered at `src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx:385-428`), composed by server-run data sources.

The enforcement evidence is the `manage_entity`/`manage_entity_schema` server tools the hooks call (`src/lib/api/entities.ts:603,676,700`), which are data-driven, not per-type endpoints. A **GUESS-free** check: creating a new entity type via `EntityTypeForm` (`src/components/settings/entity-types/entity-type-form.tsx:76`) makes a new list screen, detail screen, edit form, and sidebar entry appear with zero frontend code (sidebar: `src/components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx:346-433` lists `useEntityTypes` dynamically).

## 3. Form / list-view / filter builders, column chooser, saved views, admin CRUD

- **Form builder: YES (flat)** — `SchemaBuilder` (`src/components/settings/entity-types/schema-builder/schema-builder.tsx:173`), visual + raw-JSON modes. Visual mode is explicitly restricted to a flat object of primitives + enums (`isSimpleSchema`, `schema-builder.tsx:40-55`); nested objects/arrays/`oneOf` force JSON mode (`schema-builder.tsx:318-325`). No conditional/grouped layout, no line-item child schema.
- **List-view builder: PARTIAL** — the table/board/gallery switcher is a fixed built-in set plus authored `view_templates` (server-stored), but there is **no visual builder** for those templates (they're JSON authored server-side), and the switcher override is **session-only, never persisted** (`entity-type-list-panel.tsx:102` "session-only — never persisted").
- **Column chooser: NO** — columns = whatever the schema marks `x-table-column`; no per-user show/hide/reorder/width. Only the board has a group-by column toggle (`src/components/entities/entity-board-view.tsx:377`).
- **Filter builder: NO for entity lists** — a single free-text search box (`entity-type-list-panel.tsx:413-418`) + server-side sort; no field filter builder, no saved filters. The rich `clf_*`/`ClassificationFilters` machinery (`src/lib/filter-utils.ts`, `src/lib/event-filters.ts`) applies **only** to the Events stream, not entity lists.
- **Saved views: NO** — nothing persists a list configuration.
- **Admin CRUD scaffold: YES for types** — create/edit/delete/audit-history of entity types (`src/components/settings/entity-types/entity-type-page.tsx:25`, `:98` history) and relationship-type rules (`src/components/settings/entity-types/relationship-types-tab.tsx`). This is the nearest thing to a "resource admin".

## 4. Adding a new screen — two paths and touch points

**Schema-driven path (the one that matters for 441 screens):** define a new entity type at `/$owner/memory?create_type=true` → `EntityTypeForm` → server `manage_entity_schema`. The list (`/owner/<type>`), detail (`/owner/<type>/<slug>`), edit form, sidebar entry, schema-graph node all render automatically. **Touch points in `packages/owletto`: 0 code files.** (Verified end-to-end in code: route at `$entityType/index.tsx`, panel at `entity-type-list-panel.tsx`, form at `dynamic-schema-form.tsx`, detail at `entity-tabs/index.tsx`.)

**Hand-built path (for Lobu's own sections):** a concrete example is the agent guardrails screen (`src/app/$owner/agents/$agentId/guardrails/*.tsx`). Files that must change:
1. Route file(s) under `src/app/$owner/…` using `createFileRoute` (auto-registered into `src/routeTree.gen.ts` by the TanStack router plugin — `tsr.config.json`).
2. Page component(s) — e.g. `src/components/agents/agent-guardrails-index.tsx`.
3. API hooks in `src/lib/api/*.ts` via `createOrgQuery`/`createMutation` (`src/lib/api/hook-factory.ts`) naming a server tool.
4. Nav wiring — `OWNER_SECTIONS` in `src/lib/owner-sections.ts` + the sidebar in `src/components/sidebar/app-sidebar.tsx`.
5. A smoke-test case in `src/app/__smoke__/all-routes.test.tsx` (route param fixtures + expected text, `all-routes.test.tsx:30`).
6. (Server, out of scope) a corresponding tool registration in `packages/server`.

So a bespoke screen is ~5–6 touch points of hand-written React; a schema-driven screen is zero.

## 5. Data-entry ergonomics

- **Keyboard-driven grid entry: NO.** `EntityTableView` is read-only (sort + paginate + link out); editing is a separate sidebar form. No cell editing, no Enter-to-move-between-cells, no explicit tab order (browser default DOM order only; the one `tabIndex` in the entities dir is the graph view, `entity-type-graph-view.tsx:625`).
- **Inline add/edit rows: PARTIAL.** Single-record edit via the sidebar `DynamicSchemaForm` (save disabled until dirty, `entity-tabs/index.tsx:86,256`). Board drag = inline "move", `entity-board-view.tsx`. Click-to-edit primitives exist (`src/lib/editable-field/editable-primitive.tsx:40`) but are wired for agent-correction flows (`onCorrection` in `JsonRenderer`), not the entity grid. No inline "add row to a grid".
- **Master-detail (header + lines): NO.** Entities are flat records with JSONB `metadata`; `parent_id`/children give a hierarchy (parent column in list, `entity-table-view.tsx:403`), and typed relationships are **displayed read-only** (`src/components/memory/entity-relationships-panel.tsx:12-17` — "what IS linked, not what MAY be"). There is no editable line-item grid (no document header + lines pattern anywhere in the generic surface).
- **Lookup/autocomplete pickers: PARTIAL.** The generic form offers only an enum `<Select>` (`dynamic-schema-form.tsx:211-245`). A generic `Combobox` exists (`src/components/ui/combobox.tsx`) but only bespoke screens use it (member-picker, connector-selector, model-selector). Tables can *display* cross-linked entities (`x-link-entity-type`, `entity-table-view.tsx:201`) but the form cannot *pick* a related entity — no entity lookup control.
- **Validation display: PARTIAL.** Required-marker `*` + disabled Save (`dynamic-schema-form.tsx:217`, `entity-tabs/index.tsx:256`); server errors surface in a red box (`create-entity-form.tsx:166`). No per-field error annotations, no format/length/range checks client-side.
- **Unsaved-change guards: NO.** Dirty state only disables the Save button; there is **no** `beforeunload`, route blocker, or confirm-on-leave anywhere (grep for `beforeunload|useBlocker` = zero matches).

## 6. Printing and document output

**NO.** No PDF generation, no print layouts, no report templates, no Excel/CSV import or export anywhere in `packages/owletto`. The only `.pdf` string is a test fixture attachment (`src/mcp-apps/review/main.tsx:103`). The chart/data-table widgets render on-screen only; there is no download/serialize path. (Charts exist: `src/lib/json-renderer/charts/*`, ECharts-based.)

## 7. Localization / i18n

**NO.** No translation layer, no i18n library in `package.json`; all UI strings are hard-coded English literals in components. Locale is hard-coded `en-US` for dates in the two generic renderers (`src/components/entities/entity-table-view.tsx:593`, `src/lib/json-renderer/format-value.ts:58`). A Turkish UI would be a from-scratch extraction pass (feasible; purely mechanical, ~200 component files).

## 8. Offline / latency / optimistic updates

**NO offline mode, NO optimistic mutations.** Data is react-query with modest stale times (30s list, 60s type — `src/lib/api/entities.ts:671,760`), SSE-driven invalidation (`src/lib/use-invalidation-sse.ts`), and server-side sort/pagination/search (list params in `useEntitiesByType`, `entities.ts:603`). All writes await `mutateAsync` and flip `isPending` (no `onMutate`/`setQueryData` anywhere in `src/lib/api`). The single exception is the board's drag: optimistic move with per-entity rollback on error (`entity-board-view.tsx:409-412`). Nothing survives offline; an ERP's latency-sensitive data entry is fully server-round-trip.

---

## VERDICT

| Capability | Rating | Effort to close gap |
|---|---|---|
| Schema-driven list/grid renderer (arbitrary type) | **YES** | exists; extend for ERP → MECHANICAL |
| Schema-driven form renderer | **PARTIAL** (flat scalars; no lines/lookups/date/image) | **HARD** |
| Form/list-view/filter builders, column chooser, saved views | **PARTIAL** (flat form-builder only; no list/filter/chooser/views) | **HARD** |
| Adding a screen without hand-written React | **YES** (0 files per schema-defined type) | TRIVIAL (mechanism exists) |
| Data-entry ergonomics (keyboard grid, inline rows, master-detail, lookups, unsaved guards) | **NO** (single-record edit + read-only relations only) | **HARD** |
| Printing / PDF / Excel | **NO** (no infra at all) | **HARD** |
| i18n / Turkish UI | **NO** (hard-coded English, `en-US` dates) | MECHANICAL |
| Offline / optimistic updates | **NO** (server-round-trip writes; board-only optimistic) | MECHANICAL |

**Bottom line.** The decisive precondition — "screen renders from a schema, not from hand-built code" — is met in kind and in production shape: 441 Prodma screens would not be 441 React files, they'd be ~441 entity-type/schema/template definitions plus data. But the generic form and grid are **flat-scalar only**: no master-detail line grids, no entity-lookup fields, no per-field filters, no column chooser/saved views, no keyboard grid entry, no unsaved-change guards, no PDF/Excel, no Turkish. Those are buildable additions on top of the existing `JsonRenderer`/`DynamicSchemaForm`/`EntityTableView` foundation and **conflict with no documented AGENTS.md invariant** (nothing is ARCHITECTURAL). The honest answer: *structurally feasible as a schema-driven app builder, and a long way short of transactional ERP depth today.* The hard core of the gap is one thing — there is no generic "document with editable line items" abstraction — and nearly every other NO (filters, chooser, saved views, lookups, grid editing) hangs off that missing master-detail primitive. **(GUESS:** I did not run the app; all findings are from reading the shipped code paths above, which are consistent and well-tested.)**

# Lobu capability audit — aggregates vs. the no-read-path-aggregation invariant

Scope: can an ERP's aggregate layer (customer balance, stock on hand, AR aging, trial balance, order backlog) be built on Lobu when AGENTS.md forbids aggregating history on user-facing read paths and mandates write-time materialization? Ratings are against the Prodma bar (money exact and reproducible). Evidence is code + `db/migrations/*.sql`; speculation is marked **GUESS**.

## 1. The write-time materialization pattern exists — in three real, shipped shapes

The pattern AGENTS.md sanctions ("Materialize the row or counter at WRITE time and read it back by index" — AGENTS.md:15) is real code, not a slogan. Three end-to-end examples:

- **Running "latest" folded into the row** — `latest_eval_score` / `latest_eval_at` / `latest_eval_run_id` on `watchers`. Materialized at write: the same `sql.begin` transaction that inserts the per-metric `eval_score` events also does `UPDATE watchers SET latest_eval_score = …, WHERE id = … AND (latest_eval_run_id IS NULL OR latest_eval_run_id <= $runId)` (packages/server/src/runs/eval-scores.ts:480-516) — the WHERE is a monotonic guard so an OLD run scored late (another replica, later queue tick) cannot regress the stamp. Read back by index: the column is in the queryable `watchers` schema (packages/server/src/utils/table-schema.ts:518), so a reader selects the row and never touches the score events. Companion: per-case rolling window `metadata.recent_scores`, capped at 20, read-modify-write under `FOR UPDATE` with run_id dedupe (eval-scores.ts:582-613).
- **Atomic running counter** — `rate_limit_counters` (db/migrations/20260610130000_rate_limit_counters.sql): `count` maintained by one atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE SET count = count + 1 RETURNING count` per request; read back by exact `(key, window_start)` PK. The migration comment is explicit this exists to defeat per-pod in-memory counters. UNLOGGED by design — drift-accepting abuse control.
- **Write-time derived index** — `entity_identities` (db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1075): a normalized `(org, namespace, identifier) → entity_id` claim row INSERTed at write time (packages/server/src/auth/subject-identities.ts:51-69, packages/server/src/tools/save_content.ts:394-402), live-unique (baseline:3678), read by exact lookup. And `events.superseded_by`, dual-written in the same tx as the superseding INSERT (packages/server/src/utils/insert-event.ts:616-623) so the read path is a plain `WHERE superseded_by IS NULL` view (db/migrations/20260702300020, current shape db/migrations/20260807130000:60-102) instead of a per-row anti-join.

Every one of these is a specific, hand-authored counter/row tied to a specific feature. **None is a general mechanism.**

## 2. The decisive question — can a NEW aggregate be defined at runtime without code + migration? PARTIAL, and only the read-time kind

Two runtime-definable aggregate surfaces exist; both are READ-TIME SQL, both require an owner/admin (not an agent), neither materializes anything:

- **Derived entity types (`backing_sql`)** — an owner/admin calls `manage_entity_schema` with `{ backing: { sql, connection? } }`; `entity_types.backing_sql` is a typed column (db/migrations/20260529130000_entity_types_backing.sql), set via INSERT/UPDATE (packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:504, 623-627). No migration. A derived type is "derived iff backing_sql IS NOT NULL"; measure/dimension roles are classified ON READ from the SQL (packages/server/src/utils/infer-measures.ts:1-12, `measureColumns` at manage_entity_schema.ts:428). Rows are produced by running `backing_sql` through the `query_sql` executor (packages/server/src/utils/entity-management.ts:75-98) — read-time SQL, `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY`, 5s timeout (packages/server/src/tools/admin/query_sql.ts:629-631). Trigger-enforced: a derived type can never hold stored rows, and a populated type can never become derived (db/migrations/20260531120000_reject_rows_on_derived_types.sql).
- **Declared metrics (`metrics_config`)** — `entity_types.metrics_config` jsonb holds eventSets/measures/dimensions/segments (db/migrations/20260615120000_entity_types_metrics_config.sql:6-12; the migration comment: "The future metric compiler lowers this into backing SQL; this migration only adds the storage"). `query_metric` compiles the measure to a GROUP BY SELECT and runs it read-only (packages/server/src/metrics/run-metric.ts:59-76; packages/server/src/tools/admin/query_metric.ts). The compile step is `SELECT … FROM (SELECT * FROM events WHERE …) … GROUP BY entity_id, dims` (packages/server/src/metrics/compiler.ts:99-141) — i.e. **read-time aggregation over the event stream**, not a materialized counter.
- **View templates** (admin-authored, structurally validated, versioned) back their data sources through the same read-only, org-scoped `executeDataSources` executor (packages/server/src/utils/execute-data-sources.ts:951-1092), so a template's aggregate is also read-time SQL.

So the honest answer: a new **number** can be defined at runtime by an admin with no code change — but only as a query that re-aggregates history on every read. A new **materialized counter** cannot: every materialized counter in §1 is feature code plus a migration. There is no declarative "define a counter/rollup over events and have the platform maintain it" surface anywhere (`query_sql` is strictly read-only; the only write tool is `manage_entity`, which writes entity rows, not counters). **GUESS** on nothing here — the two surfaces above are the complete set of aggregate-definition tools in packages/server/src/tools/admin.

Gate note: `manage_entity_schema` create/update/delete are OWNER_ADMIN actions (packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:82-88); `query_sql`/`metric_series`/`query_metric` are read-tier for members (tool-access.ts:242). So an agent cannot self-serve a new aggregate type; it must be an admin, or the agent must act through an admin session. `manage_entity_schema.ts:412-418` even documents why derived counts are skipped on the type-get endpoint: "Derived counts run the full backing SQL (multi-second on large event tables) and this endpoint is called on every entity page open."

## 3. Derived types / `backing_sql` / declared metrics — read-time SQL, and how that squares with the invariant

All three are read-time. The "square" is a documented, deliberate exception:

- The metric compiler is explicit about being the sanctioned exception: "Consolidation: the `aggregate` step (SELECT agg(expr) … GROUP BY dims) is the SAME step a federated warehouse metric flows through" (compiler.ts:9-12); `validateAndScopeQuery` rewrites `events` → `current_event_records` (superseded masked) and org-scopes it (run-metric.ts:67-70; the rewrite in packages/server/src/utils/execute-data-sources.ts:597-653). It runs `GROUP BY` over the event view on a user-facing read path — exactly what AGENTS.md:15 nominally forbids — as the one sanctioned aggregation surface.
- **The invariant has no technical enforcement.** Nothing in `query_sql` (query_sql.ts:377-726), `metric_series` (packages/server/src/tools/admin/metric_series.ts:141-282), `executeDataSources`, or `validateAndScopeQuery` rejects `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT` over `events`. The only DB-layer enforcement near this space is the append-only guard (db/migrations/20260610040000_events_append_only_guard.sql) — which stops DELETEs, not aggregations. A derived view's `backing_sql` may `GROUP BY` over `events` freely, org-scoped by the CTE. So the invariant is a review-time rule, not a platform property.
- v1 limits make the exception smaller than it sounds: `eventSet.by: "alias"` and `reads: "current"` only — `"window"`/`"link"`, `"raw"`, and `{ asOf }` throw `MetricNotImplementedError` (compiler.ts:62-79); `factIdentity` (cross-source dedupe) is deferred in the SDK contract (packages/connector-sdk/src/metrics.ts:36-66). `agg` is capped to sum/count/min/max/count_distinct (compiler.ts:146-167).

So: the sanctioned path for a *governed* number is read-time SQL with a curated vocabulary; everything is live aggregation of a masked stream, never a stored total.

## 4. Drift detection and repair — NO

- There is no reconcile step that re-derives any materialized value from its source. `latest_eval_score` is written once per scoring and never recomputed from the score events; the eval scorer queue (`packages/server/src/scheduled/score-eval-runs.ts`) is a completion queue, not a drift checker: its predicate is "terminal run with no live `eval_score` event yet" (score-eval-runs.ts:94-100) — it fills MISSING scores, it does not verify STORED ones. The `superseded_by` stamp was filled historically by a one-time script (db/migrations/20260702200000_events_superseded_by.sql:40 comment references `scripts/backfill-superseded-by.ts`); no periodic reconciliation re-runs it.
- The one genuinely drift-tolerant surface is `rate_limit_counters`, and its drift is *by design*: UNLOGGED so a PG crash resets windows, exactly like a pod restart (20260610130000:15-20).
- For ERP money, "silent drift" would mean a stored balance disagrees with its posting history and nothing notices. There is no checksum/recompute/historic-replay job in `packages/server/src/scheduled/` that re-sums source rows into a stored counter. The pattern for exactness is absent — not because it conflicts with an invariant (a write-time counter recomputed by a migration/backfill is exactly the sanctioned shape, AGENTS.md:15), but because nothing ships it.

## 5. Backdated writes and recompute — NO

- The substrate accepts retroactive `occurred_at` freely: `insertEvent` takes a caller `occurredAt` and defaults to now only when omitted (insert-event.ts:72-78, 506). Nothing validates an event into a "period", and there is no period/close concept at all (no period table, no close flag — consistent with the sibling data.md report §6).
- Because the only materialized aggregates are not time/period-based (`latest_eval_score` is run-keyed; `rate_limit_counters` is wall-clock abuse control; `entity_identities` is current identity), no materialized running total can be invalidated by a backdated posting today. The moment an ERP adds one (running-average stock cost, AR balance), a backdated posting changes the sum of everything after it — and there is **no recompute trigger, no invalidation hook, no "replay history from point X" primitive**. `insertEvent`'s only post-insert hooks are `afterPersist` and the embedding/lineage writes (insert-event.ts:625-631) — nothing aggregate-aware. The sanctioned answer (run the recompute "in a migration, never per request", AGENTS.md:15) exists as a prescription, not as a mechanism.
- The entity write path itself is non-transactional by comparison: `manage_entity.ts` contains no `sql.begin` (its create/update use bare `getDb()` calls), so a composite document write (header + lines + counter updates) has no provided all-or-nothing container — the ERP author must assemble `sql.begin` themselves (the primitive exists at 132+ sites; see the sibling atomicity.md).

## 6. Point-in-time queries ("balance on 31 March") — NO (governed), PARTIAL (hand-rolled SQL)

- Declared but not implemented: the SDK contract advertises `MetricReadMode = 'current' | 'raw' | { asOf: string }` where `{ asOf }` compares against `occurred_at` (packages/connector-sdk/src/metrics.ts:21-27) — and the compiler throws `MetricNotImplementedError` for anything but `"current"` (compiler.ts:71-76). So "customer balance as of 31 March" is not answerable through `query_metric`.
- What the data would support: `events` carries both `occurred_at` (event time) and a supersede chain, so a hand-written `query_sql` could approximate an as-of state by filtering `occurred_at <= <date>` over a masked stream. But nothing maintains per-period balances, nothing snapshotts a period's totals, and `current_event_records` masks by *system-time supersession*, not by posting period — so an as-of reconstruction is one-off SQL each time, exact only if the author gets the supersede masking + event-time semantics right. **GUESS** on the owletto UI surface (bundle not in this worktree).

## 7. Conclusion — does write-time materialization work for ~500 entity types and hundreds of aggregates?

- The pattern works and is the *only* ERP-correct shape in this codebase, but it is **a developer discipline, not a platform capability**. Each counter needs a migration, a write-path hook, and a monotonic/locking story like eval-scores.ts:498-506. At ~500 entity types with hundreds of distinct aggregates (per-customer AR, per-item stock, per-period totals), the runtime-definable surfaces (§2) only produce read-time SQL that either violates the invariant (cheap to define, costly forever) or the ERP author writes a materializer per number (correct, but a developer per number).
- The invariant and runtime-definability are in direct tension: AGENTS.md forbids the one kind of aggregate you can define at runtime, and the kind it mandates (write-time counters) is exactly the kind that requires a developer. That tension is the architectural gap — it is not resolved by an infinitely capable agent, because no amount of cleverness makes a read-time GROUP BY over a growing append-only table cheap or turns a declarative metric declaration into a maintained counter. An agent can *ask* for a number; it cannot make a stored running total that stays correct under backdated writes, or detect that one drifted.

## VERDICT

| Capability | Rating | Gap-close effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Write-time materialization pattern | YES (three shipped shapes; all feature-specific) | — |
| 2. Define a new aggregate at runtime, no code | PARTIAL (read-time SQL only via backing_sql/metrics_config, owner-admin; no materialized-counter definition) | ARCHITECTURAL (a declared-counter/matview surface) |
| 3. Derived types / backing_sql / declared metrics | PARTIAL (read-time SQL, sanctioned exception, v1-only: alias/current, 5 aggs; no `asOf`/link/window) | MECHANICAL (finish compiler modes) |
| 4. Drift detection / reconciliation of materialized values | NO (completion queues only; no re-derive or checksum) | MECHANICAL (per-counter reconcile job) |
| 5. Recompute after backdated / prior-period writes | NO (no period concept, no recompute/invalidation hook) | HARD (period ledger + replay primitive) |
| 6. Point-in-time aggregate ("balance as of date") | NO governed (`asOf` declared, NotImplemented); PARTIAL hand-rolled SQL | MECHANICAL (implement `asOf` read mode) |
| 7. Materialization workable for ~500 types / hundreds of aggregates | NO without a developer per number (runtime surface only produces read-time SQL) | ARCHITECTURAL |

Bottom line: the write-time materialization pattern is proven and is the only invariant-correct shape — but it is hand-authored per number, and the only runtime-definable aggregates are read-time SQL that the invariant nominally forbids. The agent's competence cannot close this: the gap is a platform mechanism (declared, write-maintained counters with a recompute path) that does not exist.

===== atomicity.md =====
# Atomicity — where deterministic, transactional business logic can run

Scope: every context that can run org-specific logic, and whether any of them can
hold a DB transaction spanning multiple entity writes. ERP test: price/tax/posting/
costing rules are deterministic code, and a posting must be all-or-nothing.

## 1. Execution contexts — can each open a transaction / take a lock?

| # | Context | Org code? | Multi-write DB tx? | Lock? | Time / memory / call limits | DB access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Sandbox (`run_sdk`/`query_sdk`) — `packages/server/src/sandbox/run-script.ts` | Yes, esbuild-compiled TS in an isolated-vm V8 isolate | **No.** Each `client.*` dispatch is a separate host-side call; writes autocommit per call (`run-script.ts:936-1014`) | Only the `FOR UPDATE` a host handler takes inside its own single-statement tx | memory 8–64 MB (clamped, `run-script.ts:344-352`); wall-clock 1–180 s (`MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `run-script.ts:162`); 200 SDK calls max (`sdkCallQuota`, `run-script.ts:155`); 4 MB/message, 64 KB logs | `client.query` only: read-only, see §3 |
| B | Sandbox namespaces (entities, feeds, behaviors, connections…) — `packages/server/src/sandbox/namespaces/*` | Writes go to platform admin handlers | No — per-call autocommit | No caller lock | Same as A | Org-scoped, handler-governed |
| C | Behavior reaction scripts — `packages/server/src/watchers/reaction-executor.ts:74-82` | Yes, same sandbox, `userId:null` system tier | **No.** Runs post-commit of the window (see §5) | No | 60 s default (`reaction-executor.ts:22`) | Same SDK as A |
| D | Behavior declared outputs — `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_behaviors/complete-window.ts:575` | **No code.** Org supplies `extracted_data` + a declarative `outputs` schema on a versioned, admin-validated template | **YES** — one `sql.begin` spans canvas event + content links + entity promotion + classifications + run transition + schedule advance (`complete-window.ts:575-1017`) | Partial-unique indexes + savepoints | n/a | Full platform tx |
| E | Connector sync/action code — org-installed compiled code via `installConnector`/`updateConnectorSource` (`manage_connections/handlers/connector-management.ts`), run by `@lobu/connector-worker/executor/runtime.ts` | Yes | **No — the child process has no DB handle at all.** Env allowlist is 7 keys, no credentials (`connector-worker/src/executor/subprocess.ts:127-142`); `ExecutorJob`/`ExecutorResult`/`ExecutionHooks` carry no db surface (`connector-worker/src/executor/interface.ts:14-168`); effects reach the DB only via `hooks.onEventChunk` → gateway `insertEvent` | No | 10 min default, 512 MB old space (`subprocess.ts:151-154`) | None. HTTP egress + chrome dispatch only |
| F | Operations `local_action` — `tools/admin/manage_operations/handlers/execute.ts:142` (`executeCompiledConnector`) | Yes — same connector child | Same as E | No | Same as E | None |
| G | Operations `http_operation` / `mcp_tool` | No org code, outbound calls | No | No | 120 s fetch timeout (`operations/execute-http-operation.ts:6,83-116`) | None |
| H | Server code | Org cannot add any | Platform-only (`sql.begin` at 132 non-test sites, per brief) | `pg_advisory_xact_lock` at 63+ sites | n/a | Full |

**What "yes" would need.** A transaction is a property of one host process/connection.
Contexts A–C are in the gateway process but each SDK dispatch is stateless (no tx
handle threaded across calls); E/F are child processes with no DB; G has no code.

## 2. THE CENTRAL QUESTION — the finding

> Is there ANY context where an org can run its own deterministic code inside a
> transaction that spans multiple entity writes?

**No. There is no such context.** Every org-code path is exactly one of:

1. V8 sandbox where each `client.*` call is its own host transaction (autocommit).
   A posting implemented as "update debit, update credit, update stock, bump
   counter" is **4 independent transactions**. A crash after step 2 leaves the
   org in a half-posted state an agent cannot repair atomically.
2. A connector child process with **no DB handle** (`subprocess.ts:127-142`).
   Connector code cannot even open one write.

The one place a multi-entity write *is* atomic — Behavior declared outputs flowing
through `complete-window.ts:575` → `promote-keyed-entities.ts` — is reached only by
**data**, never by org code: the org contributes `extracted_data` rows and a schema;
all decision logic is the platform's (`promote-keyed-entities.ts:296-431`: stable-key
upsert, policy gates, savepoints). There is no seam for "price = qty × rate;
validate; post" to run inside that transaction. Everything else the brief's ERP
needs (running-average cost, gapless numbering, double-entry) has no home.

This is not solvable by an agent being clever: atomicity is the property the
platform owns, and an agent calling `client.entities.update` N times cannot get
one rollback boundary.

## 3. The sandbox's DB surface

`client.query(sql)` (`packages/server/src/sandbox/client-sdk.ts:239-270`) is the only
direct SQL an org script can run:

- **Read-only, twice enforced**: `isReadQuery` (`utils/execute-data-sources.ts:231-233`)
  + explicit "Only SELECT / WITH queries are allowed" (`execute-data-sources.ts:358-360`).
- **Org-scoped**: every referenced table is wrapped in an org-scoping CTE
  (`buildScopedQuery`, `execute-data-sources.ts:408-416`); auth/identity tables are
  admin-only (`restrictedTables`, `client-sdk.ts:250-253`).
- **Bounded**: runs in `sql.begin` + `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` + `SET LOCAL
  statement_timeout = '5000'` (`client-sdk.ts:262-266`); result capped at 5 000 rows
  (`CLIENT_QUERY_MAX_ROWS`, `client-sdk.ts:30`).
- The transaction opens and closes inside that single call. It cannot be held open
  across two `client.query` calls, and it can't write.

Writes exist only as named SDK methods (`entities.create/update/link`, …) that
dispatch to platform handlers — see §1B.

## 4. Idempotency primitives (retried op must not double-post)

All primitives are **per-primitive**, none spans a multi-write business transaction:

- **Events, connector dedup**: `insertEvent` holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on
  `(connection_id, origin_id)` then supersede/insert (`utils/insert-event.ts:645-653`,
  `events_webhook_ingest_dedupe` unique index). Guarantees one current row per
  connector item across replicas.
- **Events, audit**: `_lobu_idempotency_key` unique per org
  (`idx_events_org_idempotency_key`), used by `insertConnectionlessAuditEvent`
  (`insert-event.ts:697-704`) and the Behavior change-set
  (`complete-window.ts:873-916`).
- **Runs**: `action_idempotency_key` partial-unique + `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`
  (`runs/queue-service.ts:1177-1181`); also `runs_idempotency_key_uniq` for
  behavior/watcher runs. A re-execute of the same operation key returns the prior
  run (`execute.ts:332-396`).
- **Entities**: Behavior entity outputs claim a stable-key identity via
  `entity_identities` `ON CONFLICT … WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`
  (`utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:385-394`).
- **Numbering**: `getNextNumericId` = `MAX(id)+1` under a per-table advisory lock
  (`tools/admin/helpers/db-helpers.ts:133-144`), but is **hard-coded to 3 internal
  tables** (`watchers`, `watcher_window_events`, `watcher_versions`) — not usable by
  org code for per-year invoice numbers, and org code can't be in its transaction.

Two retries of the same "post" that each touch *different* rows (new event ids,
new counter) both succeed — no primitive re-derives the whole posting.

## 5. Failure mid-sequence: compensation, saga, dead-letter?

**None of the above.** There is no outbox, saga engine, or DLQ in the server
(grep for `outbox|saga|dead.?letter|DLQ` finds nothing but retry/redelivery for
signal delivery). Concretely:

- `recordChangeEvent` — the audit row after an entity edit — is **fire-and-forget**
  (`insert-event.ts:755-787`: `retryWithBackoff(...).catch(drop)`). The entity
  `UPDATE` committed in `updateEntity`'s tx (`entity-management.ts:616`) and the
  event commit independently (`manage_entity.ts:547`); a crash between them loses
  the audit row silently.
- Behavior reactions run **post-commit** of the window. `complete-window.ts:1116-1165`
  retries the reaction 3× then reports `reaction_status:'failed'`; the canvas and
  promoted entities are already committed. Any writes the reaction performed before
  failing stay. **Partial state is the normal outcome.**
- A failed operation run flips `runs.status='failed'` (`execute.ts:45-56`); partial
  side effects of a half-run connector/action are not compensated.

The platform is careful *inside* the code it fully owns (`complete-window` rollback,
queued run+approval-event one tx, `execute.ts:624-707`), but org code has no such
boundary and no recovery mechanism.

## 6. Concurrency: two users posting to the same stock item

Nothing serialises a **multi-entity** posting today:

- Single-entity writes do serialize: `updateEntity` does `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` +
  merge + `UPDATE` in one tx (`entity-management.ts:616-624`), so two concurrent
  updates of the *same* entity row are last-writer-wins on a fresh read. Good but
  per-row only.
- A stock running-average computed as "read item → compute → write item" is safe
  per item, but a posting touching *several* rows (item + counter + related
  entities) has no shared lock: interleaving is possible between the separate
  handler transactions.
- `entity_relationships` link does a **check-then-insert** without a serializing
  lock (`manage_entity.ts:1504-1560`).
- `getNextNumericId`'s advisory lock is the only cross-row serialization primitive
  and is locked to internal tables (see §4).

## 7. Smallest change that gives org logic a transaction boundary

Option 1 — **thread a tx handle through the sandbox**: give the guest a
`client.tx(async () => …)` whose body dispatches SDK calls onto one
`sql.begin`/connection. Conflicts:
- **Wall-clock/call budgets**: 180 s / 200 calls (`run-script.ts:162,155`) make a
  long-lived open transaction hostile; `client.query` already caps statements at 5 s.
- **Multi-replica invariant**: a tx is node-local. The sandbox runs on whatever
  replica serves the request; it cannot migrate a half-open tx to another replica,
  and per-replica pool connections can't be pinned across replica switches. Root
  `AGENTS.md` forbids shared state in in-memory Maps — a live tx is exactly that.
- Every handler currently takes `getDb()` itself; retrofitting a caller-supplied
  `sql` (as `insertEvent`/`queue-service` already accept via options) means touching
  every namespace handler and every nested call, and the `entity-merge`/policy paths
  would silently read the pool, not the tx.

Option 2 (much smaller, and the pattern that already works) — **extend the
declarative path, not the code path**: generalize Behavior *declared outputs* into
a platform-side "atomic action" that compiles a JSON-Schema action definition into a
`sql.begin` body (like `complete-window.ts:575` + `promote-keyed-entities.ts`), and
let a sandbox reaction *invoke* it as one atomic SDK call instead of issuing N
separate writes. The org supplies declarative rules (formulas/keyed fields); the
platform owns the transaction, so atomicity is guaranteed by construction.

Conflicts with documented invariants:
- Option 1: violates the spirit of "no cross-replica shared/required state in
  memory" and the fail-closed dispatch model (`run-script.ts:689-697`); needs a new
  session-affinity guarantee the SSE/queue architecture doesn't have.
- Option 2: conflicts with nothing in `AGENTS.md`; it is additive. It does *not*
  give orgs arbitrary code in a transaction (that's Option 1), so price/tax rules
  must be expressible declaratively. A true "run my TS inside your tx" is
  ARCHITECTURAL.

## VERDICT

- Sandbox can run org code: **YES**
- Org code inside a multi-entity-write DB transaction: **NO** — ARCHITECTURAL
- Multi-call transaction in the sandbox (threaded tx handle): **NO** — HARD
- Org code with a DB handle at all (connector child): **NO** (by design; worker
  credentials invariant) — BY DESIGN
- Read-only, org-scoped SQL from sandbox: **YES**
- Behavior declared-output multi-write atomicity (platform path): **YES** (PARTIAL
  for org control — data-in, no code)
- Idempotency (per-primitive: events/entity-identity/run key): **YES** — but for a
  full posting as one unit: **PARTIAL** — MECHANICAL to extend
- Failure compensation / saga / DLQ for org multi-write: **NO** — ARCHITECTURAL
- Cross-entity concurrency serialization for a posting: **NO** — HARD
- Declarative "atomic action" primitive (Option 2): not present — MECHANICAL/HARD

===== authz.md =====
# Lobu capability audit — authorization, identity, multi-tenancy

Scope: can Lobu express ERP-grade access control (Prodma-style `YETKI_ALANLAR` field grants, operation-level rights, row/owner scoping, statutory audit) — or where does it structurally fall short? Evidence from `db/migrations/*.sql`, `packages/server/src/auth`, `packages/server/src/authz`, `packages/server/src/tools/admin`, `packages/owletto/src`. Every YES is cited to enforcement code, not just schema.

## 1. What the permission model IS today

- **Tenant root = organization; everything is org-scoped first.** `organization` is "the tenant root. Every other table scopes to an organization" (db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1742-1759). The enforcing boundary is `MultiTenantProvider.resolveAuth`: for session/PAT/OAuth/worker-token callers it resolves the requested org by slug and requires a `member` row — no membership ⇒ 403 (`packages/server/src/workspace/multi-tenant.ts:132-691`, membership check at 239-247, 403s at 494-502 and 619-648). PATs are additionally hard-bound to one org — a PAT minted for org A is rejected against org B even if the owner belongs to both (multi-tenant.ts:451-461).
- **Roles: exactly three values, per (org, user).** `member.role ∈ {owner, admin, member}` (baseline:1577-1589; `packages/owletto/src/hooks/use-members.ts:5`). There is no group or role registry; `member` is the junction and its comment calls it "the auth source of truth for permission checks at the org level" (baseline:1589).
- **Human authorization = coarse role-tier × MCP scope, per tool+action.** Three access levels — `read | write | admin` — computed by `getRequiredAccessLevel` from three hand-maintained action matrices (`PUBLIC_READ_ACTIONS`, `MEMBER_WRITE_ACTIONS`, `OWNER_ADMIN_ACTIONS`, `packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:13-271`). Enforcement is centralized and called from both boundaries: `enforceRoleScopeAccess` (`packages/server/src/tools/access-control.ts:66-88`) is invoked per action by the REST/MCP tool dispatch (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/action-router.ts:34-35`) and by the tool registry boundary (`packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:636`). A token additionally needs `mcp:read`/`mcp:write`/`mcp:admin` scope (`hasRequiredMcpScope`, tool-access.ts:282-305); session-cookie callers are role-gated only.
- **Everything beyond role-tier is a different, narrower axis, not general authorization.** The write-gate (`write_approval_policies`) governs only **non-human** writes; the ACL gates (`member_of` resource membership) govern only **connector-sourced content reads**, opt-in per connection. Neither is a general per-user ERP permission engine. Detail in §2–§4.

## 2. Field-level read masking ("warehouse sees stock, not unit cost") — **NO**

- The ONE field-level read redaction in the product is hardcoded to a single field on a single type: `redactMemberEmail` strips the `$member` entity's email field from `get`/`list` for non-admin/owner users (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:615-627`, applied only when `e.entity_type === '$member'` at 1093-1103 and 1294-1304). It is not driven by any permission table — it is an `if (role === admin) show email else hide` in code.
- Every generic read seam returns full entity metadata to any member: `manage_entity.get/list` (manage_entity.ts:1095-1128), recall/`get_content` (metadata included in the row projection, `packages/server/src/tools/get_content/behavior-mode.ts:450`), and **raw SQL**: `query_sql` is "member-safe" — any member can `SELECT entities.metadata` (which carries every field, incl. a hypothetical `unit_cost`) inside the schema-validated allowlist; only `oauth_tokens`, `oauth_clients`, `user` are admin-restricted (`packages/server/src/utils/table-schema.ts:826-828`, `packages/server/src/tools/admin/query_sql.ts:570`). Connection config is redacted, but entity metadata is not (table-schema.ts:422-437).
- The write-gate DOES carry a `field_path` scope (`db/migrations/20260709120000_write_policy_expand.sql`) — but that is **write approval/deny for agents**, not read masking for humans, and humans bypass it entirely (§3). `docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md` (the whole authz program) is about chat/source channel-repo ACLs and does not plan field-level grants either.
- Gap-close effort: **HARD** — would need a per-(role|user, entity-type, field) read-grant table plus threading a projection into `manage_entity`, `get_content`, `query_sql`, and every derived view. There is no existing mechanism to hang it on; the one redaction precedent is hardcoded.

## 3. Operation-level permissions for a specific user — **NO** (agent-scoped write-gate only)

- The write-gate `write_approval_policies` (expanded 2026-07-09/10/11: `db/migrations/20260709120000_write_policy_expand.sql`, `20260710120000_write_policy_action_effects.sql`, `20260711100000_write_policy_operation_key.sql`) is a real per-action `auto|approval|deny|disabled` engine, scoped global → entity type → field → single entity → connector operation. **But its principal axis is `agent | watcher` only** (`PolicyPrincipalKind = "agent" | "watcher"`, `packages/server/src/authz/entity-policy.ts:54`; `normalizePrincipalKind` coerces anything else to null, entity-policy.ts:188-190).
- **Humans are explicitly out of the write-gate's scope by design:** "Human edits are never gated here — role restrictions for humans live in the tool-access tier" (entity-policy.ts:14-15); `evaluateEntityMutation` returns `allow` for `principalKind === "user"` (entity-policy.ts:796); `evaluateEntityFieldUpdates` allows every field for users (entity-policy.ts:976-979); `resolveWriteEffect` returns `auto` for users (entity-policy.ts:883). The gate pipeline (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-mutation-gate.ts:179-181`, `approval-interceptor.ts:240-243`) therefore never denies or defers a human's write based on any per-user rule.
- So a human member's write rights are exactly the three-tier action matrices (§1): `manage_entity.create/update/link/unlink` are member-write; `delete/merge/resolve_duplicates/unmerge` owner-admin (tool-access.ts:23, 81). A per-user grant/deny of one specific operation (e.g. "can post a purchase order but not approve it") is not expressible.
- Enforcement points for the tiers that DO exist: `enforceRoleScopeAccess`/`getRequiredAccessLevel` at `action-router.ts:34-35` and `registry.ts:636`; `manage_connections` handler additionally gates member edits on `created_by === ctx.userId` (tool-access.ts:26-34, handler re-check). Connector `execute` is write-tier but re-gated per-principal by connection visibility and the agent-only connector_action policy (`tool-access.ts:53-66`; `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations/handlers/list-available.ts`).
- Gap-close effort: **HARD** — adding a user-principal axis to the write-gate is additive (accept `user` in `PolicyPrincipalKind`, route the human write path through `runMutationGate`), but doing it *correctly* means changing the invariant "human edits are never gated here" and reworking the tool-access tier, which is the documented architecture today.

## 4. Row-level scoping / ownership beyond org — **NO** (three narrow, opt-in exceptions)

- **General per-user row predicates: none.** There is no `WHERE created_by = $user`-style scoping on entity reads, no per-user data partition, no tenancy below the org. A sales rep can read every customer entity in the org.
- Exception A — **connection-sourced rows**: `compileConnectionFkVisibility`/`compileConnectionRowVisibility` hide events/feeds/connections that are `visibility='org'` OR the requester's own (`created_by`) (`packages/server/src/authz/connection-visibility.ts:41-78`). This applies to the *connection recall/query seams* only, not to entity records themselves.
- Exception B — **resource-membership ACL, opt-in and off by default**: Slack/GitHub ACLs are synced into `member_of` edges (`packages/server/src/authz/access-graph.ts`), then `channel-visibility.ts:214-263` (chat) and `resource-visibility.ts:62-135` (connector events) filter reads to members of the `$resource`/channel — **but only once a connection has a fresh `authz_source_acl_state` row** (channel-visibility.ts:14-22); a never-graphed connection keeps the legacy all-members behavior. Scope is resources ("repo/channel"), not ERP rows ("customers"), and the whole program (`docs/plans/authz-acl-permission-program.md:40-110`) is explicitly a connector-source ACL, not an ERP ownership model.
- Exception C — `$member` email redaction (§2), role-based, not row-based.
- Gap-close effort: **ARCHITECTURAL** for a general model — AGENTS.md forbids new tables/DB design without sign-off; a per-row owner predicate on arbitrary entity types would be a new cross-cutting authorization layer (the `member_of` machinery is the natural substrate but is not keyed to user-defined ERP types today).

## 5. Approval workflows / delegation / "operation owner" — **PARTIAL**

- A durable approval plane EXISTS and is in production: agent/watcher writes that policy or human field-ownership blocks are **deferred into a `runs` row (`approval_status`) + an `interaction_type='approval'` event card**, grouped per watcher window (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/entity-field-approval.ts:627-746`; deferral builders in `approval-interceptor.ts`). Approve/reject is a first-class tool (`manage_operations.approve/reject/approve_batch/reject_batch`, tool-access.ts:60-66).
- **"Operation owner" exists in a narrow sense.** Field ownership (`field_controls` marks human-owned values; `entity-policy.ts:1000-1007` forces approval when a non-human writes a human-owned field) plus the recorded `action_input.owner_user_id` give the *field owner* the right to decide their own run: `requireApprovalAuthority` allows admin/owner, else only the run's recorded field owner (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_operations/handlers/approvals.ts:725-796`). Approval itself requires a verified human web session — agents can never approve (`approvals.ts:759-774`).
- **No delegation, no escalation, no multi-step chains.** "Owner" is the proposing context's recorded user; there is no "approver" assignment, no substitute/delegate, no threshold-based routing (e.g. "PO > 50k goes to finance"), and — because humans bypass the write-gate (§3) — the approval plane never triggers on a human-entered over-limit transaction.
- Gap-close effort: **HARD** — the machinery (durable run + card + notify) is reusable; what's missing is routing rules that fire on *human* writes and an approval-assignment model, which again needs the §3 user-principal work.

## 6. Users, roles, groups + admin management — **PARTIAL**

- Users: `user` + `account` (better-auth, baseline:1983, 327); org membership: `member` (§1); invitations: `invitation` (baseline:1520). Every user is auto-provisioned a personal org at signup (`packages/server/src/auth/personal-org-provisioning.ts`, wired at index.tsx:887-906). **Groups: none** — no `teams`/group table exists despite the organization plugin's "teams support" flag (index.tsx:300-301; no teams table in any migration).
- Admin UI: member **listing** exists (`packages/owletto/src/hooks/use-members.ts:31-40` via `organization.listMembers`). **No invite / role-change / remove UI** was found anywhere in `packages/owletto/src` (grep for `updateMemberRole|createInvitation|inviteMember|removeMember` = 0 hits) — the better-auth organization endpoints exist server-side but are not surfaced in the app; role changes today ride the API/hooks in `packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:521-557` (audited there). Permissions configuration UI exists for **agent** write policies (`packages/owletto/src/components/agents/agent-permissions-route.tsx`, `agent-permissions-matrix.tsx` — admin-only, per entity-type/per-field action effects).
- Gap-close effort: TRIVIAL (invite/role UI) to MECHANICAL (groups) — better-auth's organization plugin is already wired; groups need a new table + membership model.

## 7. Authentication — **YES** (broad), **NO** for SAML/LDAP

- Methods, all in one better-auth config: email+password (`packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:200-229`), magic link (index.tsx:720-779), phone OTP over WhatsApp/Twilio (index.tsx:782-815), WebAuthn/passkey (index.tsx:835-850), OAuth social + generic-OIDC/OAuth2 login providers driven by `connector_definitions.login_enabled` (index.tsx:98-147, 291-293) — Slack/Google/GitHub today, any OIDC issuer addable per-org via a login-enabled connector. Session model: better-auth cookie sessions, 7-day expiry, daily sliding update (index.tsx:279-282), plus bearer-plugin session tokens (index.tsx:299). API auth: `owl_pat_*` PATs (`db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1797`; `packages/server/src/auth/tokens.ts`), OAuth 2.1 access tokens (`packages/server/src/auth/oauth/`), and signed worker tokens for agents.
- **SAML / LDAP / SCIM / Active Directory: NO.** No reference anywhere in `packages/server/src` or `packages/core/src` (grep `saml|ldap|scim|active directory|kerberos` = 0 hits). Enterprise IdP would have to be OIDC/OAuth2 or be added.
- Gap-close effort: SAML/SCIM → **HARD** (new plugin + IdP metadata + SCIM provisioning endpoints); nothing else needed.

## 8. Audit trail — **PARTIAL** (good for updates/schema/lifecycle; not a WORM ERP audit log)

- **`events` is append-only at the DB layer** — a BEFORE DELETE trigger blocks every non-cascade delete (opt-out is transaction-scoped `SET LOCAL lobu.allow_event_delete`; `db/migrations/20260610040000_events_append_only_guard.sql`). This gives tamper-evident *history* for everything that lands in `events`.
- **Who-changed-what-when with before/after DOES exist for entity updates.** `manage_entity` diffs old vs new name/slug/parent/metadata and records `semantic_type='change'` events carrying `metadata.changes = [{field, old, new}]`, `created_by`, `entity_ids` (`packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity.ts:492-556`, via `recordChangeEvent`, `packages/server/src/utils/insert-event.ts:672-787`). Content values are masked as `"[changed]"` (manage_entity.ts:520-522).
- **Gaps that disqualify it as a *complete* legal log:**
  - Entity **create and delete by humans record no change event** — `recordChangeEvent` appears only on the update path (manage_entity.ts:547); create/delete handlers emit none (create path manage_entity.ts:250-360; delete path has no audit call). The `entities` row is mutated in place; there is no entity-field version history — the dedicated `entity_field_state` projection trigger has "no producer" (db/migrations/20260622150000:13-16).
  - **`events` rows are UPDATEd in place**, not immutable: the append-only guard blocks DELETE only, and live code stamps conversation metadata and flips `interaction_status` on approval rows (e.g. `packages/server/src/gateway/routes/internal/interactions.ts:119-131`; `superseded_by` stamping in insert-event.ts). An auditor cannot rely on "once written, never changed."
  - The change audit is **fire-and-forget with best-effort retry**; a double failure logs `'audit trail is missing this row'` rather than blocking the mutation (insert-event.ts:774-786). No cryptographic chaining/tamper-evidence beyond append-only.
  - What IS covered well: schema (entity-type) changes — `entity_type_audit` with `before_payload`/`after_payload`/`actor` (baseline:1242-1251; written in `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:228`); org/member/invitation/agent/connection lifecycle via `recordWorkspaceChangeEvent` (`packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:317-638`, `insert-event.ts:828-921`); and every agent-write approval decision (pending→approved/rejected rides `runs` + interaction events).
- Gap-close effort: **MECHANICAL** to close the create/delete gap (mirror the update-path diff writer) and add entity field history; **HARD** for true WORM/chain-of-custody (the append-only invariant explicitly permits in-place UPDATE today).

## 9. Constraints on an ERP deployment from the credentials/workers rules

- **Workers never receive real credentials — only placeholders/proxied access** (root AGENTS.md; `packages/server/AGENTS.md:29-34`; `packages/agent-worker/AGENTS.md:7`). Worker egress goes through an authenticated gateway proxy with `WORKER_ALLOWED_DOMAINS` allow/deny (`packages/agent-worker/AGENTS.md:20-21`). Consequence for an ERP: **no agent/worker can hold a SQL Server connection, a provider API key, or the ERP's own service credential** — every data touch must be mediated by gateway code that swaps placeholders at egress. The only durable-credential carve-outs are device-pinned connectors and ~1h provider-derived *leases* (server AGENTS.md:31-34) — deliberately no static-credential tier.
- **Secrets storage exists but is gateway-owned**: `agent_secrets` (encrypted, baseline:406-419) + the secret/MCP proxy. An ERP's ERP-side credentials (e.g. e-Fatura API keys) would have to live there, never in a worker.
- Related invariants an ERP must respect: cross-pod state must be Postgres-mediated (no in-memory singletons, server AGENTS.md:37-41); `events` append-only (§8); request paths never aggregate history (no `GROUP BY`/`DISTINCT ON` over `events`/run-history on user-facing reads — directly relevant to ERP reporting); and no new tables/DB design without sign-off.

---

## VERDICT

| Capability | Rating | Effort to close gap |
|---|---|---|
| Org-scoped multi-tenancy + membership enforcement | **YES** (`member` junction, 403 at resolveAuth) | — |
| Role-based permission model | **YES** (owner/admin/member × read/write/admin tiers + mcp:* scopes) | — |
| Field-level read masking (`YETKI_ALANLAR`) | **NO** (one hardcoded `$member`-email redaction only) | **HARD** |
| Operation-level per-user grant/deny | **NO** (write-gate is agent/watcher-only; humans bypass it by design) | **HARD** |
| Row-level scoping / owner predicates beyond org | **NO** (opt-in `member_of` resource ACLs on connector content only) | **ARCHITECTURAL** |
| Approval workflow + "operation owner" | **PARTIAL** (durable approval cards, admin-or-field-owner decide; no delegation/escalation, humans never gated) | **HARD** |
| Users / roles / groups | **PARTIAL** (users+3 roles+invitations yes; no groups) | MECHANICAL |
| Admin-manage users & permissions from UI | **PARTIAL** (member list + agent-permission matrix; no invite/role-change screen) | TRIVIAL |
| Authentication breadth | **YES** (password, magic link, OTP, passkey, OAuth/OIDC, PATs, OAuth 2.1) | — |
| SSO / SAML / LDAP / SCIM | **NO** (OIDC/OAuth2 only; zero SAML/LDAP/SCIM code) | **HARD** |
| Legally defensible audit log | **PARTIAL** (append-only events + update/schema/lifecycle diffs; create/delete unaudited, rows mutable, best-effort writer) | MECHANICAL→HARD |
| ERP viability under credentials/worker rules | **PARTIAL** (agents can't hold real credentials; gateway must mediate every data path) | **HARD** |

**Bottom line.** Lobu is a *tenant-isolated, role-tiered, agent-centric* authorization model. What an ERP needs that it structurally lacks is the **principal axis for humans**: no per-field read grants, no per-user operation grants, no row-owner predicates — the write-gate is explicitly "never gated for humans," and the only field-level masking is one hardcoded email redaction. The durable-approval plane and the `member_of` resource gate are real and production-shaped but are pointed at agent writes and connector content, not ERP transactions. Nothing here violates an AGENTS.md invariant by itself, but a general per-user ERP permission layer on top of the role-tier + agent-write-gate split is a **HARD** re-derivation of the authorization architecture, not an additive feature; row-level scoping over user-defined ERP entities is **ARCHITECTURAL**. **(GUESS flag:** no live app run; every claim is from the cited enforcement code and migrations, which are consistent and heavily cross-referenced; the owletto "no invite/role-change UI" finding is grep-based.)

# Lobu capability audit — data modelling, integrity, transactions

Scope: can Lobu's storage substrate host a traditional transactional ERP (Prodma-style: 503 tables, posted documents, gapless numbering, corrections)? Evidence from SQL migrations (`db/migrations/*.sql`, 237 files, ~18k lines, 103 `CREATE TABLE` statements including dropped) and server code. "`entities`" here = the row store, "`events`" = the append-only log; the two are distinct.

## 1. Record store separate from `events`; typed fields — PARTIAL

- **Separate store: YES.** `entities` (db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:1016) is a row table, NOT the events log. Its COMMENT (baseline:1040) is explicit: "Domain objects tracked per organization… the row body is jsonb keyed by the type's columns." `entity_types` (baseline:1275) holds per-org type definitions with `metadata_schema jsonb`. Relations: `entity_relationships` (baseline:1204), `entity_identities` (baseline:1075), `entity_relationship_types` (basel…15922 tokens truncated…ent dedup, FOR UPDATE for specific rows) — correct for *ingest*, absent for *two people editing the same invoice field*.

Gap-close effort: **MECHANICAL** (row `version` column + 409 on mismatch, plus a per-replica or Postgres-based invalidation fan-out — e.g. LISTEN/NOTIFY, which the runs-queue already uses).

## 9. Deployment — YES (on-premise is supported, not a special case)

- **Self-host is first-class**: `docker-compose.example.yml` (pgvector + app image `ghcr.io/lobu-ai/lobu-app`, workspaces volume, healthchecks; the published image is the same artifact Lobu Cloud runs) and docs/DOCKER.md; a full **Helm chart** for Kubernetes (`charts/lobu/`, deployment.yaml with readiness/liveness, PVC, PDB, migrations Job). The data plane is entirely the customer's Postgres — no data leaves except LLM-provider calls and (optional) remote runtime compute.
- **Required external dependency is the LLM provider** for agent features (ANTHROPIC/OPENAI/etc. keys, docker-compose.example.yml) — the same cloud dependency as the ERP vendor's own hosted service; for a customer refusing *any* third-party cloud, an on-prem/private LLM endpoint can be configured, but that is **GUESS** (the code reads provider base URLs from config, but I did not verify every egress path). `ENCRYPTION_KEY` + `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` are required and local.
- **Single-node / air-gapped shape exists**: embedded Postgres + embedded connector-worker for `lobu run` / the Mac app (packages/server/src/embedded-runtime.ts; scheduled/embedded-connector-worker.ts). Scale is not a constraint at <20 users; the architecture (Postgres-mediated multi-replica state, AGENTS.md:36-41) degrades gracefully to one process.

Gap-close effort: **TRIVIAL** (the compose/Helm path exists); verify the air-gapped LLM story before promising zero external calls.

## VERDICT

| Capability | Rating | Gap-close effort |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Write operations (define/validate/expose; single-op transactional) | PARTIAL (full op surface + AJV + approval + idempotent durable runs; no multi-op tx) | MECHANICAL (multi-op tx); ARCHITECTURAL (saga) |
| 2. Aggregation / reporting | PARTIAL (write-time materialization is the design; ad-hoc SQL + declared metrics exist; no report catalog/UI, v1 metric limits) | MECHANICAL–HARD |
| 3. Scheduled work (recurring + reliability + heavy batch) | PARTIAL (cron/behaviors/feeds at-least-once with idempotency; small bounded work units, no fan-out) | MECHANICAL |
| 4. Long-running / multi-step (saga) | NO (choreography via Behaviors only; no saga/compensation engine) | MECHANICAL (choreography); ARCHITECTURAL (saga) |
| 5. Files & documents | PARTIAL (inline attachments + ephemeral 24h artifact store; no PDF/doc generation) | MECHANICAL (durable files); HARD (document stack) |
| 6. External integration w/ credentials | YES (connectors + http_operation + MCP; AES-GCM secrets; worker placeholder proxy) | TRIVIAL–MECHANICAL |
| 7. Bulk data import (millions of rows) | NO (Postgres read-only connector 5k/sync, webhook 120/min, no SQL Server/CSV loader) | MECHANICAL (loader); ARCHITECTURAL (ERP data plane) |
| 8. Realtime + stale-write detection | PARTIAL (SSE cache-invalidation, best-effort cross-pod; no optimistic locking) | MECHANICAL |
| 9. On-premise deployment | YES (compose + Helm + embedded; LLM-provider egress is the only external dependency) | TRIVIAL |

Bottom line: as an *orchestration + integration layer*, Lobu is genuinely strong — a durable, idempotent, approval-gated operation fabric, write-time materialization, at-least-once scheduling, encrypted secrets with a hard worker/credential boundary, and first-class self-hosting. As a *traditional ERP host*, it is **NO today**: no multi-step transactional posting or saga, no report/documents stack, no bulk migration path, no optimistic concurrency, and aggregation is deliberately SQL + materialized rather than a report engine. Every gap is additive (none collides with a documented invariant), but the ERP layer — posting, statutory numbering, e-Fatura documents, report delivery, a 503-table data plane — is product to be built, not configuration. A credible short-term stance: Lobu as the workflow/integration/reporting front-end *around* an ERP (or around a fresh ERP data plane in `entities`+`events`), not as the ERP itself.

# Lobu capability audit — JsonRenderer extensibility (custom UI components)

Scope: can Lobu's JSON→UI renderer host ERP screens the generic vocabulary can't express (editable invoice line grid, stock-movement matrix, aging report) as **registered** components rather than hardcoded ones? Evidence from `packages/owletto/src/lib/json-renderer/`, `packages/owletto/src/components/entities/`, `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_view_templates.ts`, `packages/server/src/utils/validate-json-template.ts`, `packages/server/src/utils/execute-data-sources.ts`, `packages/server/src/tools/resolve_path.ts`, `packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts`, `db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql`.

## 1. The JSON→UI node contract

`JsonNode` is a five-variant tagged union (`packages/owletto/src/lib/json-renderer/types.ts:79`):

- **`text`** `{type:'text', content}` — a literal string (types.ts:6-9).
- **`data`** `{type:'data', path, fallback?, format?}` — binds a value by path; `format` is a display directive (`currency|date|url|enum|boolean|number|text`, types.ts:11-22, 92-100). Path lookup is dotted + array-indexed (`user.name`, `items[0].title`) via `getValueByPath` (renderer.tsx:434-444). A leaf `data` becomes a click-to-edit `EditablePrimitive` only when the caller supplies `onCorrection` (renderer.tsx:467-475) — no caller does today.
- **`if`** `{type:'if', condition, then, else?}` — truthy path lookup selects the branch (types.ts:65-70; renderer.tsx:489-498).
- **`each`** `{type:'each', items, as, render}` — iterates an array, binding `as` and `asIndex` into a child context; `render` may be a node or a `"- {{t}}"` string shorthand (types.ts:72-77; renderer.tsx:501-524).
- **`component`** `{type: string, props?: Record<string,unknown>, children?: JsonNode[]}` — the only extensible variant; `type` is `ComponentType | (string & {})` so **any string is a legal node type** (types.ts:55-63). `props` may also ride flat next to `type` (flat DSL + `props` bag merge, reserved keys `type/children/props/path/fallback/key` dropped, renderer.tsx:569-592).

Prop resolution per node (renderer.tsx:539-562): `"@name"` → the matching action from `context.actions`; pure `"{{path}}"` → typed value; `"{{a}}/100"` → string interpolation. Non-function `on*` handlers are dropped with a console warn (renderer.tsx:582-590). A `table` node carrying resolved `data` (array) + `columns` is special-cased into a sortable/paginated read-only `WebTable`/`DataTable` (renderer.tsx:597-606; data-table.tsx:145-492 — **no cell editing, no row add/remove**).

Type→component resolution is a two-level lookup at render time (renderer.tsx:530-531):

```
const Component = context.components?.[node.type] ?? componentRegistry[node.type];
```

Unknown type → `console.warn` + render `null` (renderer.tsx:533-536). Both registry levels must satisfy `RendererComponent = React.ComponentType<{children?, className?, [key:string]: unknown}>` (types.ts:181-185).

## 2. The registry — static, import-time, app-code-only

- **Base registry**: a module-level `const componentRegistry` in renderer.tsx:57-330. Not exported; extended only by editing the source.
- **App-level registry**: `entityRendererComponents` — a static module-level object literal (packages/owletto/src/components/entities/renderer-registry.tsx:144-150). It is imported by exactly one caller, `entity-type-list-panel.tsx:30`, and passed as `<JsonRenderer components={entityRendererComponents} …/>` at entity-type-list-panel.tsx:475-480.
- **No runtime registration exists.** There is no `register()` API, no dynamic `import()` of component bundles, and no plugin/connector/org supply path — a zero-hit grep across `plugin-api`, `plugin-host`, `connectors`, `agent-worker`, `core` for any component-registration surface. `componentRegistry` is resolved via `context.components` — but `context.components` is populated only by whatever the **caller module hardcodes**. A connector/org can author a *template* (data, see §5) referencing any type string, but the node renders only if the shipped bundle happens to contain a component with that name.
- **Consumers are inconsistent**: the entity **list** panel passes the registry, but the entity **detail** page (`packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/index.tsx:407,416,424`) and the event card (`packages/owletto/src/components/entity-tabs/events-tab/event-card.tsx:2266`) render `<JsonRenderer>` with **no `components` prop** — an authored template referencing `entity-table`/`entity-board` renders `null` there. The schema-derived auto-default avoids this only because it uses base vocabulary only (packages/server/src/utils/default-entity-template.ts:68-101).

## 3. Full built-in node vocabulary

Base registry (renderer.tsx:57-330): `div, span, p, h1, h2, h3, h4, ul, ol, li, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td`; card family `card, card-header, card-title, card-description, card-content`; widgets `badge, button, alert, alert-title, alert-description, progress, separator, markdown`; layout `layout, columns, metric`; charts `bar-chart, line-chart, area-chart, pie-chart, sparkline, stacked-area-chart`. Structural node types handled outside the registry: `text, data, if, each`.

App registry (renderer-registry.tsx:144-150): `entity-avatar, entity-link, entity-table, entity-board, metric-series`.

Note: the zod `componentTypeSchema` enum (types.ts:109-139) is a **stale subset** (missing `layout/columns/metric` and all chart types) — it is not the enforcement path; `jsonNodeSchema` accepts any `z.string()` type (types.ts:145-170).

## 4. Adding an `invoice-lines` component today — touch points

1. Write the React component (new file under `packages/owletto/src/components/`).
2. Import + add a key to `entityRendererComponents` (renderer-registry.tsx:144) — one line.
3. To reach the detail page and event-card surfaces, also pass `components` at the **4 additional call sites** that currently omit it: entity-tabs/index.tsx:407, 416, 424; event-card.tsx:2266.
4. For writes, wire an action: the only actions any caller supplies today are `updateEntity` + `openCreate` on the list panel (entity-type-list-panel.tsx:389-395); the detail page and event card pass **no `actions` at all**, so a save-capable grid there has nothing to bind.
5. Rebuild + redeploy the owletto SPA bundle — **a deploy is required** for the component itself. The *template* that invokes it is then authored at runtime by an admin (see §5), no deploy.

## 5. Authoring, sandboxing, security model

- **Who may author**: only the `owner`/`admin` role. `manage_view_templates` `set/rollback/remove_tab/clear` are admin-tier (packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:170); `get` is public-read (tool-access.ts:203); members never write (asserted in tool-access.test.ts:174-176). `verifyAccess` re-checks the resource belongs to the caller's org (packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_view_templates.ts:107-154). Templates are org-scoped rows, never shared.
- **Three authoring paths**, all funneling into the same admin-gated handler: the `manage_view_templates` MCP/REST tool (manage_view_templates.ts:51-64), the ClientSDK `viewTemplates` namespace (packages/server/src/sandbox/namespaces/view-templates.ts:49-62), and the `lobu apply` declarative config `viewTemplate` key (packages/cli/src/commands/_lib/apply/map-config.ts).
- **Template sandboxing — structural only, no component allowlist (deliberate)**: `validateJsonTemplate` runs at set-time and rejects malformed node shape, missing required fields, unknown `format`, and handler props that don't bind `"@actionName"` (packages/server/src/utils/validate-json-template.ts:44-174). The component `type` string is **explicitly not allowlisted** "so the renderer can't be coupled to the server" (validate-json-template.ts:11-16). Render-side the template is inert data — no `eval`, component resolution is the §2 allowlist, unknown types render null, and non-function handlers are dropped (renderer.tsx:533-536, 582-590).
- **`data_sources` are the real sandbox**: named SQL queries nested in a template are validated at save (SELECT/WITH only, forbidden ops, admin tables rejected, entity-type slugs resolved) and at read run in a `READ ONLY` transaction with a 5s timeout, org-scoped CTE wrapping, schema-qualified refs rejected, secret columns masked, `MAX_ROWS = 1000` (packages/server/src/utils/execute-data-sources.ts:72-74, 902-930, 971-1092).
- **Where templates come from**: `view_template_versions.json_template` (jsonb) + `view_template_active_tabs` for named tabs, both org-scoped (db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:2042-2051, 2075-2088). `resolve_path` resolves entity-instance-over-type via `COALESCE(vtv_entity.json_template, vtv_et.json_template)` (packages/server/src/tools/resolve_path.ts:523-531), executes `data_sources` server-side at read time, strips the key from the returned template, and returns `template_data` (resolve_path.ts:298-343, 630-633). No template → auto-default synthesized from the type's metadata schema (resolve_path.ts:676-697; default-entity-template.ts:50-103).

## 6. Versioning — YES, real

Append-only, gapless per scope: every `set` inserts a new `view_template_versions` row with `version = MAX(version)+1` keyed on `(resource_type, resource_id, organization_id, tab_name)` — unique `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (baseline.sql:3186-3191; manage_view_templates.ts:196-215). A default-template `set` re-points the parent's `current_view_template_version_id` FK (`entities` baseline.sql:1027/4796; `entity_types` 1289/4922; update at manage_view_templates.ts:219-225); a named-tab `set` upserts `view_template_active_tabs.current_version_id` (manage_view_templates.ts:226-236). `rollback` re-points the same FK/pointer to a historical version (manage_view_templates.ts:384-466); `remove_tab` deletes only the tab pointer, version rows stay (468-507); `clear` nulls the parent FK (352-382). Full history is queryable via `get` (273-343). Entity-type mutations emit a config-audit event; per-entity templates are runtime data, deliberately not config-audited (89-104).

## 7. The key question — smallest credible change for third-party components

Today, "registering" a component means editing an import-time object literal in the frontend bundle. The pieces that are already right: the DSL accepts any node type string, `context.components` already overrides the base registry, the server already validates structure + sandboxes `data_sources`, and admins can author templates at runtime without a deploy. The gaps are (a) the component itself must be compiled into the bundle, (b) the `components` prop isn't threaded to every renderer call site, and (c) the action surface is hardcoded per caller.

- **In-repo custom component (closest today)**: write the component + one registry line (+ thread `components` to the 4 detail/event call sites + add a save action if interactive). **MECHANICAL**, but requires a frontend deploy. For an editable invoice grid this also needs the caller to supply save/line-ops actions, which is a new server mutation contract — the renderer contract already supports `"@actionName"` binding, the callers just don't supply the actions a form needs.
- **True org-specific/third-party runtime components**: a new org-scoped component-bundle registry (DB row or config) mapping node type → served JS module, returned by `resolve_path` like `data_sources` today; the frontend `import()`s the bundle and feeds its exports into `components` at every call site. The bundle must share the app's single React instance (must not bundle React). Authoring gate = owner/admin (same as templates; client JS is unsandboxable in the browser regardless, and the server already treats template-authoring admins as trusted for arbitrary SQL). **HARD**, not ARCHITECTURAL: nothing in AGENTS.md forbids it — the binding constraints are only the ordinary ones (new DB/API surface needs sign-off; a served bundle needs a delivery/versioning story; every JsonRenderer call site must receive the map).

Even fully implemented, a registered `invoice-lines` node still can't be an ERP data-entry grid on the **detail page today**, because that surface supplies no `actions` — the binding contract is call-site-hardcoded, not template-declared.

| Component-type resolution via caller-supplied registry override | **YES** (renderer.tsx:530-531, `context.components`) | — |
